title: Give runners a build identity and stale-code detection
goal:
Give runners a build identity and stale-code detection
Source: docs/tasks/b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c/RESPONSE.md WP-A (cause N1), RESPONSE_SURVEY.md q15. Parent bug: task b3401f19.

Evidence (RESPONSE.md N1): local-bravo (pid 256984, booted 2026-11-12 11:51:20) runs with cwd /home/server/projects/kainbain/runner -- the ENGINE's own git checkout, currently on branch kb/b3401f19... runner/daemon.js and runner/modelDiscovery.js on disk have mtime 11:51:24, 4s AFTER boot; runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js does not exist there, and on-disk refreshDiscoveredModels returns early when config.models is pinned. runner/version.json has said 0.1.0 since 2026-10-31 and all runners report versions.runner 0.1.0, so no runner can tell it runs stale code and the self-updater never fires. This is why many past tickets "fixed it" yet nothing changed. Confirm: RESPONSE.md section 3.3 commands.

Files owned: runner/version.json, the release/publish script that writes it (scripts/ publish path used by runner/updates), runner/daemon.js factsFor().versions ONLY, api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js (versions passthrough), Settings runner card (frontend/src/components/settings/...Runner...). NOTE: WP-B also touches runner/daemon.js but only refreshDiscoveredModels/boot -- rebase whichever merges second.

Change: (1) Add build {sha, builtAt, dirty} to runner version, stamped at publish/bundle time; dev runners from a git checkout compute sha at boot (git rev-parse HEAD + dirty from git status --porcelain runner/). (2) Heartbeat facts.versions adds build + bootedAtMs; runner hashes its runner/ tree at boot and re-hashes cheaply (mtime scan) per heartbeat, reporting codeChangedSinceBoot:true when files changed after boot. (3) Publish pipeline bumps runnerVersion on every release touching runner/** or api/agent/harnesses/** (CI check fails the release if not) so runner/updates can offer updates. (4) Settings runner card shows build sha + warning when build.sha != backend sha or codeChangedSinceBoot.

Survey constraints: round-2 q15 -- warn, never block, on version mismatch ("Only block stale runners if there is a version incompatibility").

Acceptance: unit test asserting factsFor() reports build identity (fails today); codeChangedSinceBoot flips after a file touch (temp-dir fixture); normalizeCapabilities preserves versions.build; Settings warning renders; release CI rejects unbumped version when runner code changed. Sequencing: no blockers; blocks WP-F.

# Values

## User understandable over technical language

I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible

### Principles

- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
- File structure should reflect the call stack
- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
- Include why things are done not just what is done
- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
  
  

## Functional over Object oreintated

Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

### Principles
- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.



# Inspirations
My principles here are inspired by:

- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
- Life isn’t binary (book)
- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)


# Examples

## Intent Driven descriptions

### Bad Example

```js

const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {

    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}

    users.push(user)
  
}

const list = []

userFactory("Frank",32,list)


```

## Good example

```js

/**
* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
*/
const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
  
  return ageNextYear
}

const userObjectsList = []

const usersName = "Frank"
const usersAge = 32

const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})

userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})


```

Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

### Principles
- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.



# Inspirations
My principles here are inspired by:

- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
- Life isn’t binary (book)
- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)

## Intent Driven descriptions

### Bad Example

```js

const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {

    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}

    users.push(user)
  
}

const list = []

userFactory("Frank",32,list)


```

## Good example

```js

/**
* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
*/
const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
  
  return ageNextYear
}

const userObjectsList = []

const usersName = "Frank"
const usersAge = 32

const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})

userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})


```

# Implementation Plan — Runner build identity and stale-code detection

Task: `ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084` · Parent bug: `b3401f19` · Source work package: WP-A (cause N1).
Blocks: WP-F. Shared-file coordination: WP-B also touches `runner/daemon.js` (only `refreshDiscoveredModels`/boot) — whichever merges second rebases.

## 1. Goal

Give every runner a verifiable build identity (`build { sha, builtAt, dirty }`) plus a boot-time
code hash and per-heartbeat stale-code signal (`codeChangedSinceBoot`, `bootedAtMs`), make the
release pipeline stamp and enforce version bumps so `runner/updates` can actually offer updates,
and surface a **warning (never a block)** in the Settings runner card when a runner is stale.

Why: per RESPONSE.md N1, `runner/version.json` has said `0.1.0` since 2026-10-31, all runners
report `versions.runner 0.1.0`, the self-updater never fires, and past tickets "fixed" code that
runners never picked up. A runner whose files change after boot (e.g. `runner/daemon.js` mtime
4s after boot on local-bravo) is currently indistinguishable from a fresh one.

## 2. Success criteria (acceptance, from the task)

1. Unit test asserting `factsFor()` reports build identity — fails on today's code, passes after.
2. `codeChangedSinceBoot` flips to `true` after a file touch (temp-dir fixture).
3. `normalizeCapabilities` preserves `versions.build`.
4. Settings runner card renders the warning state.
5. Release CI rejects an unbumped version when runner code changed.
6. No new blocking behavior: mismatch warns only; blocking stays limited to true version
   incompatibility (existing `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` path), per survey constraint q15.

## 3. Survey inputs (SURVEY.md + round-2 q15)

Local `SURVEY.md` (round 1, q1–q5) is **unanswered** (`"answers": {}`), and the referenced
`RESPONSE.md` / `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` parent-bug docs are not present in this checkout. The plan
therefore adopts the survey's Recommended options as explicit assumptions (flagged for
confirmation during implementation):

- q1 (what counts as incompatible): runner **major version older than required** → block only
  there; everything else warns. Matches existing minimum-version machinery.
- q2 (where the warning appears): **Settings runner card only** — no dashboard banner, no
  per-task warnings.
- q3 (code changed after boot): **warn on the card, keep running** — no auto-restart, no
  restart button in this work package (button is a named follow-up, not scope).
- q4 (dev/local runners): **show build info everywhere, warn only on managed runners**.
  Needs a managed-vs-dev discriminator (see Open questions).
- q5 (bump enforcement): **strict — fail the release** if the version was not bumped.
- Round-2 q15 (hard constraint from the task): **warn, never block, on version mismatch**
  ("Only block stale runners if there is a version incompatibility").

## 4. Guiding principle — make the change easy, then make the change

The risky parts are discovery (which files the installed runner actually reads, how the backend
record carries versions, what "backend sha" means for comparison) and test seams (`factsFor` is
currently a private function; runner tests run via `node --test`). So the workflow is:

1. **Spikes first** (Phase 0): resolve every unknown that could reshape the design before
   writing production code.
2. **Seams and fixtures** (Phase 1): extract testable units and fixtures with zero behavior
   change — pure refactors covered by the existing suites.
3. **The change** (Phase 2): five small vertical slices, each independently testable.
4. **Assurance** (Phase 3): acceptance tests, regression gates, docs, WP-B rebase, WP-F handoff.

## 5. Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; big unknowns before code)

Each spike is time-boxed and ends in a short note in this task folder (or a decision recorded
in the implementation PR). No production code here.

### Spike 0.1 — Which `version.json` does an installed runner read?

- Context: `runner/daemon.js` loads `RUNNER_VERSION`/`RUNNER_API_VERSION` from `./version.json`
  beside `daemon.js`, but `scripts/package-runner.mjs` copies `runner/` then stamps
  `<stage>/version.json` at the **archive root**. Confirm the installed layout
  (`releases/<version>/unpacked/...`) and which file the booted daemon parses.
- Outcome: the exact file the packager must stamp with `build { sha, builtAt, dirty }`, and
  whether the archive-root `version.json` needs the same stamp. If the two can diverge, the
  plan's Phase 2 slices must stamp both or unify them.

### Spike 0.2 — How do versions reach the Settings card today?

- Trace: heartbeat `facts.versions` → `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`
  (currently passes `versions` through unsanitized) → backend runner record
  (`runnerVersion` top-level? `facts.versions.runner` nested? `capabilities.versions`?) →
  `GET /runners`-style API shape → `describeRunnerVersion()` in
  `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js` (reads `runnerVersion`, else
  `facts.versions.runner`) → `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` roster/detail.
- Outcome: the exact record fields where `build` and `codeChangedSinceBoot` must land to be
  renderable, and whether backend persistence changes are needed (backend files are **not** in
  the owned-files list — if persistence changes are required, that is a scope escalation to
  resolve before Phase 2).

### Spike 0.3 — What is "backend sha" for the comparison?

- The card must warn when `build.sha != backend sha`. Find the authoritative backend identity:
  `api/version.json`? A build-info endpoint? The release manifest commit? `git rev-parse HEAD`
  at backend boot?
- Outcome: a concrete source (endpoint or field) the frontend can compare against, plus the
  old-runner/old-backend fallback (missing `build` → show "unknown", never warn — warn-only
  for *known* mismatch).

### Spike 0.4 — Managed-vs-dev discriminator (survey q4)

- Find how the backend/frontend can tell a managed runner from a dev runner today
  (install root? wrapper presence? config flag? runner id pattern?).
- Outcome: the discriminator the card uses to suppress warnings on dev runners while still
  showing build info. If none exists, the cheapest honest fallback is "warn on all" with the
  q4 refinement as a follow-up — do not invent a new registry.

### Spike 0.5 — Baseline the heartbeat test surface

- Inventory existing coverage: `runner/daemon.test.js` (pins `RUNNER_VERSION` to

  `git status --porcelain` (scoped to the packaged tree). Stamp the file Spike 0.1 proved is

  and boot sequencing; whoever merges second rebases. Prefer landing the Phase-1 extraction

2. Where does the authoritative "backend sha" live? (Spike 0.3.)

5. Does the update manifest need the build sha, or is semver comparison sufficient once bumps
   are enforced? (Slice 2.1 optional item.)

1. Spikes 0.1–0.5 (research; unblock design decisions).
2. Phase 1 seams + characterization tests (safe refactors).
3. Slice 2.1 build identity + packager stamping.
4. Slice 2.2 heartbeat signal.
5. Slice 2.3 capabilities passthrough.
6. Slice 2.4 CI bump gate.
7. Slice 2.5 Settings card.
8. Phase 3 assurance (acceptance matrix, regression, screenshots, docs, WP-B rebase, WP-F handoff).

# Implementation Plan — Runner build identity and stale-code detection

Task: `ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084` · Parent bug: `b3401f19` · Source work package: WP-A (cause N1).
Blocks: WP-F. Shared-file coordination: WP-B also touches `runner/daemon.js` (only `refreshDiscoveredModels`/boot) — whichever merges second rebases.

## 1. Goal

Give every runner a verifiable build identity (`build { sha, builtAt, dirty }`) plus a boot-time
code hash and per-heartbeat stale-code signal (`codeChangedSinceBoot`, `bootedAtMs`), make the
release pipeline stamp and enforce version bumps so `runner/updates` can actually offer updates,
and surface a **warning (never a block)** in the Settings runner card when a runner is stale.

Why: per RESPONSE.md N1, `runner/version.json` has said `0.1.0` since 2026-10-31, all runners
report `versions.runner 0.1.0`, the self-updater never fires, and past tickets "fixed" code that
runners never picked up. A runner whose files change after boot (e.g. `runner/daemon.js` mtime
4s after boot on local-bravo) is currently indistinguishable from a fresh one.

## 2. Success criteria (acceptance, from the task)

1. Unit test asserting `factsFor()` reports build identity — fails on today's code, passes after.
2. `codeChangedSinceBoot` flips to `true` after a file touch (temp-dir fixture).
3. `normalizeCapabilities` preserves `versions.build`.
4. Settings runner card renders the warning state.
5. Release CI rejects an unbumped version when runner code changed.
6. No new blocking behavior: mismatch warns only; blocking stays limited to true version
   incompatibility (existing `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` path), per survey constraint q15.

## 3. Survey inputs (SURVEY.md + round-2 q15)

Local `SURVEY.md` (round 1, q1–q5) is **unanswered** (`"answers": {}`), and the referenced
`RESPONSE.md` / `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` parent-bug docs are not present in this checkout. The plan
therefore adopts the survey's Recommended options as explicit assumptions (flagged for
confirmation during implementation):

- q1 (what counts as incompatible): runner **major version older than required** → block only
  there; everything else warns. Matches existing minimum-version machinery.
- q2 (where the warning appears): **Settings runner card only** — no dashboard banner, no
  per-task warnings.
- q3 (code changed after boot): **warn on the card, keep running** — no auto-restart, no
  restart button in this work package (button is a named follow-up, not scope).
- q4 (dev/local runners): **show build info everywhere, warn only on managed runners**.
  Needs a managed-vs-dev discriminator (see Open questions).
- q5 (bump enforcement): **strict — fail the release** if the version was not bumped.
- Round-2 q15 (hard constraint from the task): **warn, never block, on version mismatch**
  ("Only block stale runners if there is a version incompatibility").

## 4. Guiding principle — make the change easy, then make the change

The risky parts are discovery (which files the installed runner actually reads, how the backend
record carries versions, what "backend sha" means for comparison) and test seams (`factsFor` is
currently a private function; runner tests run via `node --test`). So the workflow is:

1. **Spikes first** (Phase 0): resolve every unknown that could reshape the design before
   writing production code.
2. **Seams and fixtures** (Phase 1): extract testable units and fixtures with zero behavior
   change — pure refactors covered by the existing suites.
3. **The change** (Phase 2): five small vertical slices, each independently testable.
4. **Assurance** (Phase 3): acceptance tests, regression gates, docs, WP-B rebase, WP-F handoff.

## 5. Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; big unknowns before code)

Each spike is time-boxed and ends in a short note in this task folder (or a decision recorded
in the implementation PR). No production code here.

### Spike 0.1 — Which `version.json` does an installed runner read?

- Context: `runner/daemon.js` loads `RUNNER_VERSION`/`RUNNER_API_VERSION` from `./version.json`
  beside `daemon.js`, but `scripts/package-runner.mjs` copies `runner/` then stamps
  `<stage>/version.json` at the **archive root**. Confirm the installed layout
  (`releases/<version>/unpacked/...`) and which file the booted daemon parses.
- Outcome: the exact file the packager must stamp with `build { sha, builtAt, dirty }`, and
  whether the archive-root `version.json` needs the same stamp. If the two can diverge, the
  plan's Phase 2 slices must stamp both or unify them.

### Spike 0.2 — How do versions reach the Settings card today?

- Trace: heartbeat `facts.versions` → `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`
  (currently passes `versions` through unsanitized) → backend runner record
  (`runnerVersion` top-level? `facts.versions.runner` nested? `capabilities.versions`?) →
  `GET /runners`-style API shape → `describeRunnerVersion()` in
  `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js` (reads `runnerVersion`, else
  `facts.versions.runner`) → `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` roster/detail.
- Outcome: the exact record fields where `build` and `codeChangedSinceBoot` must land to be
  renderable, and whether backend persistence changes are needed (backend files are **not** in
  the owned-files list — if persistence changes are required, that is a scope escalation to
  resolve before Phase 2).

### Spike 0.3 — What is "backend sha" for the comparison?

- The card must warn when `build.sha != backend sha`. Find the authoritative backend identity:
  `api/version.json`? A build-info endpoint? The release manifest commit? `git rev-parse HEAD`
  at backend boot?
- Outcome: a concrete source (endpoint or field) the frontend can compare against, plus the
  old-runner/old-backend fallback (missing `build` → show "unknown", never warn — warn-only
  for *known* mismatch).

### Spike 0.4 — Managed-vs-dev discriminator (survey q4)

- Find how the backend/frontend can tell a managed runner from a dev runner today
  (install root? wrapper presence? config flag? runner id pattern?).
- Outcome: the discriminator the card uses to suppress warnings on dev runners while still
  showing build info. If none exists, the cheapest honest fallback is "warn on all" with the
  q4 refinement as a follow-up — do not invent a new registry.

### Spike 0.5 — Baseline the heartbeat test surface

- Inventory existing coverage: `runner/daemon.test.js` (pins `RUNNER_VERSION` to
  `version.json`), `runner/updates-*.test.js`, `api/flow/dispatch` tests for
  `normalizeCapabilities`, `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` /
  `runnerConfigHelpers.test.js`. Note how tests construct facts today (since `factsFor` is
  unexported).
- Outcome: the seam design for Phase 1 (export vs. test hook vs. through-public-API tests).

## 6. Phase 1 — Make the change easy (zero-behavior-change refactors)

Each step must keep all existing suites green. Land as one preparatory commit (or stacked PR)
before any behavior change.

1. **Extract version loading** in `runner/daemon.js`: move the two `version.json` IIFE reads
   into a small pure loader (e.g. `loadRunnerVersionInfo(dir)` returning
   `{ runnerVersion, apiVersion, build }`) with `dir` injectable; keep `RUNNER_VERSION` /
   `RUNNER_API_VERSION` as thin wrappers. Add unit tests pinning current fallback behavior.
2. **Add a `factsFor` test seam**: export `factsFor` for tests (or add an explicit test-hook
   export) without changing its output. Add a characterization test snapshotting today's
   `versions: { protocol, runner, api }` shape — this is the test that Phase 2 extends into
   acceptance criterion 1.
3. **Add a temp-dir runner fixture helper** for runner tests: builds a fake `runner/` tree
   (with `version.json`) under `os.tmpdir()`, so the mtime-scan tests never touch the real
   checkout. Reuse in acceptance criterion 2.
4. **Frontend helper seam**: confirm `describeRunnerVersion`-style helpers are the single place
   the card reads versions from; add a pure `describeRunnerBuild(runner)` + warning-predicate
   helper file alongside with tests for the unknown/missing cases first (old runners send no
   `build` — must render "unknown", no warning, no crash).
5. **CI script seam**: verify `scripts/detect-changed-components.mjs` already flags
   `runner/**` → runner and `api/agent/**` → backend+runner (it does today, including
   `api/agent/harnesses/**`); add a test pinning that mapping so the Phase-2 bump gate can
   rely on it.

Validation after Phase 1: `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` (+ the full runner-release gate
list from `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml`), `npm run test:unit`, frontend settings
tests — all green, no behavior delta.

## 7. Phase 2 — Make the change (five slices, in order)

Slice order follows dependency order: identity → signal → passthrough → enforcement → display.
Each slice ships with its tests; each is independently revertable except where noted.

### Slice 2.1 — Build identity in `runner/version.json` + packager stamping

- Extend `runner/version.json` schema with `build: { sha, builtAt, dirty }`
  (all nullable/optional for backward compat; checked-in file carries `null`s or is
  git-ignored per repo convention — decide in implementation, document it).
- `scripts/package-runner.mjs`: stamp `build` at bundle time —
  `sha` from `git rev-parse HEAD`, `builtAt` as ISO time, `dirty` from
  `git status --porcelain` (scoped to the packaged tree). Stamp the file Spike 0.1 proved is
  read (and the archive-root copy if they differ).
- `scripts/generate-runner-manifest.mjs`: optionally carry the build sha into the manifest
  (so the update channel can compare identities, not just semver) — additive field only.
- Dev-runner fallback in `runner/daemon.js`: when the stamped `build.sha` is absent (running
  from a git checkout), compute at boot via `git rev-parse HEAD` + dirty from
  `git status --porcelain runner/`; best-effort, never fails boot (not-a-checkout →
  `sha: null`, `dirty: null`).
- Owned files: `runner/version.json`, `scripts/package-runner.mjs`

  version-loading block only.

### Slice 2.2 — Heartbeat: `build` + `bootedAtMs` + `codeChangedSinceBoot`

- Boot: record `bootedAtMs = Date.now()` and hash the `runner/` tree (cheap fingerprint:
  max mtime + file count + sizes; full content hash is overkill and slow on every heartbeat).
- Per heartbeat in `factsFor()`: re-scan mtimes cheaply (single directory walk, no hashing);

  `refreshDiscoveredModels`/boot sequencing — that is WP-B's area.**
- Performance note: the mtime walk must be bounded (ignore `node_modules`, logs); add a test
  asserting the scan completes fast on a synthetic tree.

### Slice 2.3 — `normalizeCapabilities` versions passthrough

- `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`: sanitize-and-preserve `versions.build`,

  (malformed → dropped, never a 400 — mirror `sanitizeDiscoveryStatus` bounds: capped
  strings, finite numbers, booleans).

- New script (e.g. `scripts/check-runner-version-bump.mjs`): given a base ref (default: last
  release commit, same convention as `detect-changed-components.mjs`), fail (exit 1) when
  `runner/**` or `api/agent/harnesses/**` changed but `runner/version.json` `runnerVersion`
  did not increase (semver-greater than the base's copy).
- Wire into `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml` as an early gate step (before packaging),
  reusing `detect-changed-components.mjs` path semantics so the two cannot disagree on what
  "runner code" means.
- Edge cases: first release / missing base (warn, don't fail); pre-release tags (`-rc.N`)
  count as increases over the base; `version.json`-only releases pass trivially.
- Acceptance criterion 5 test: script-level tests with fixture git ranges (or a `--files`
  mode like `detect-changed-components.mjs --files` for hermetic tests) asserting

### Slice 2.5 — Settings runner card: build sha + warning

- `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`: `describeRunnerBuild` (short sha,

  survey q1–q4: warn on known sha mismatch or `codeChangedSinceBoot`, suppress warnings for

  show short sha next to the existing version badge; render a warning banner inline on mismatch

- Copy must say what to do ("restart or update this runner") without ever disabling actions —

  per-task warnings.

  restart button in this work package (button is a named follow-up, not scope).

  Needs a managed-vs-dev discriminator (see Open questions).

  ("Only block stale runners if there is a version incompatibility").

## 4. Guiding principle — make the change easy, then make the change

The risky parts are discovery (which files the installed runner actually reads, how the backend
record carries versions, what "backend sha" means for comparison) and test seams (`factsFor` is
currently a private function; runner tests run via `node --test`). So the workflow is:

1. **Spikes first** (Phase 0): resolve every unknown that could reshape the design before
   writing production code.
2. **Seams and fixtures** (Phase 1): extract testable units and fixtures with zero behavior
   change — pure refactors covered by the existing suites.
3. **The change** (Phase 2): five small vertical slices, each independently testable.
4. **Assurance** (Phase 3): acceptance tests, regression gates, docs, WP-B rebase, WP-F handoff.

## 5. Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; big unknowns before code)

Each spike is time-boxed and ends in a short note in this task folder (or a decision recorded
in the implementation PR). No production code here.

### Spike 0.1 — Which `version.json` does an installed runner read?

- Context: `runner/daemon.js` loads `RUNNER_VERSION`/`RUNNER_API_VERSION` from `./version.json`
  beside `daemon.js`, but `scripts/package-runner.mjs` copies `runner/` then stamps
  `<stage>/version.json` at the **archive root**. Confirm the installed layout
  (`releases/<version>/unpacked/...`) and which file the booted daemon parses.
- Outcome: the exact file the packager must stamp with `build { sha, builtAt, dirty }`, and
  whether the archive-root `version.json` needs the same stamp. If the two can diverge, the
  plan's Phase 2 slices must stamp both or unify them.

### Spike 0.2 — How do versions reach the Settings card today?

- Trace: heartbeat `facts.versions` → `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`
  (currently passes `versions` through unsanitized) → backend runner record
  (`runnerVersion` top-level? `facts.versions.runner` nested? `capabilities.versions`?) →
  `GET /runners`-style API shape → `describeRunnerVersion()` in
  `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js` (reads `runnerVersion`, else
  `facts.versions.runner`) → `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` roster/detail.
- Outcome: the exact record fields where `build` and `codeChangedSinceBoot` must land to be
  renderable, and whether backend persistence changes are needed (backend files are **not** in
  the owned-files list — if persistence changes are required, that is a scope escalation to
  resolve before Phase 2).

### Spike 0.3 — What is "backend sha" for the comparison?

- The card must warn when `build.sha != backend sha`. Find the authoritative backend identity:
  `api/version.json`? A build-info endpoint? The release manifest commit? `git rev-parse HEAD`
  at backend boot?
- Outcome: a concrete source (endpoint or field) the frontend can compare against, plus the
  old-runner/old-backend fallback (missing `build` → show "unknown", never warn — warn-only
  for *known* mismatch).

### Spike 0.4 — Managed-vs-dev discriminator (survey q4)

- Find how the backend/frontend can tell a managed runner from a dev runner today
  (install root? wrapper presence? config flag? runner id pattern?).
- Outcome: the discriminator the card uses to suppress warnings on dev runners while still
  showing build info. If none exists, the cheapest honest fallback is "warn on all" with the
  q4 refinement as a follow-up — do not invent a new registry.

### Spike 0.5 — Baseline the heartbeat test surface

- Inventory existing coverage: `runner/daemon.test.js` (pins `RUNNER_VERSION` to
  `version.json`), `runner/updates-*.test.js`, `api/flow/dispatch` tests for
  `normalizeCapabilities`, `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` /
  `runnerConfigHelpers.test.js`. Note how tests construct facts today (since `factsFor` is
  unexported).
- Outcome: the seam design for Phase 1 (export vs. test hook vs. through-public-API tests).

## 6. Phase 1 — Make the change easy (zero-behavior-change refactors)

Each step must keep all existing suites green. Land as one preparatory commit (or stacked PR)
before any behavior change.

1. **Extract version loading** in `runner/daemon.js`: move the two `version.json` IIFE reads
   into a small pure loader (e.g. `loadRunnerVersionInfo(dir)` returning
   `{ runnerVersion, apiVersion, build }`) with `dir` injectable; keep `RUNNER_VERSION` /
   `RUNNER_API_VERSION` as thin wrappers. Add unit tests pinning current fallback behavior.
2. **Add a `factsFor` test seam**: export `factsFor` for tests (or add an explicit test-hook
   export) without changing its output. Add a characterization test snapshotting today's
   `versions: { protocol, runner, api }` shape — this is the test that Phase 2 extends into
   acceptance criterion 1.
3. **Add a temp-dir runner fixture helper** for runner tests: builds a fake `runner/` tree
   (with `version.json`) under `os.tmpdir()`, so the mtime-scan tests never touch the real
   checkout. Reuse in acceptance criterion 2.
4. **Frontend helper seam**: confirm `describeRunnerVersion`-style helpers are the single place
   the card reads versions from; add a pure `describeRunnerBuild(runner)` + warning-predicate
   helper file alongside with tests for the unknown/missing cases first (old runners send no
   `build` — must render "unknown", no warning, no crash).
5. **CI script seam**: verify `scripts/detect-changed-components.mjs` already flags
   `runner/**` → runner and `api/agent/**` → backend+runner (it does today, including
   `api/agent/harnesses/**`); add a test pinning that mapping so the Phase-2 bump gate can
   rely on it.

Validation after Phase 1: `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` (+ the full runner-release gate
list from `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml`), `npm run test:unit`, frontend settings
tests — all green, no behavior delta.

## 7. Phase 2 — Make the change (five slices, in order)

Slice order follows dependency order: identity → signal → passthrough → enforcement → display.
Each slice ships with its tests; each is independently revertable except where noted.

### Slice 2.1 — Build identity in `runner/version.json` + packager stamping

- Extend `runner/version.json` schema with `build: { sha, builtAt, dirty }`
  (all nullable/optional for backward compat; checked-in file carries `null`s or is
  git-ignored per repo convention — decide in implementation, document it).
- `scripts/package-runner.mjs`: stamp `build` at bundle time —
  `sha` from `git rev-parse HEAD`, `builtAt` as ISO time, `dirty` from
  `git status --porcelain` (scoped to the packaged tree). Stamp the file Spike 0.1 proved is
  read (and the archive-root copy if they differ).
- `scripts/generate-runner-manifest.mjs`: optionally carry the build sha into the manifest
  (so the update channel can compare identities, not just semver) — additive field only.
- Dev-runner fallback in `runner/daemon.js`: when the stamped `build.sha` is absent (running
  from a git checkout), compute at boot via `git rev-parse HEAD` + dirty from
  `git status --porcelain runner/`; best-effort, never fails boot (not-a-checkout →
  `sha: null`, `dirty: null`).
- Owned files: `runner/version.json`, `scripts/package-runner.mjs`
  (+ `scripts/generate-runner-manifest.mjs` if the manifest field is added), `runner/daemon.js`
  version-loading block only.

### Slice 2.2 — Heartbeat: `build` + `bootedAtMs` + `codeChangedSinceBoot`

- Boot: record `bootedAtMs = Date.now()` and hash the `runner/` tree (cheap fingerprint:
  max mtime + file count + sizes; full content hash is overkill and slow on every heartbeat).
- Per heartbeat in `factsFor()`: re-scan mtimes cheaply (single directory walk, no hashing);
  report `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` when any file under `runner/` is newer than boot (or
  the fingerprint changed). Guard cost: skip when a previous heartbeat already flipped, or
  cache scan results for N seconds.
- `facts.versions` becomes `{ protocol, runner, api, build, bootedAtMs, codeChangedSinceBoot }`
  (exact nesting per Spike 0.2 — `build` inside `versions` per the task; keep old keys
  byte-identical for old backends).
- Owned files: `runner/daemon.js` `factsFor()`/`versions` only. **Do not touch
  `refreshDiscoveredModels`/boot sequencing — that is WP-B's area.**
- Performance note: the mtime walk must be bounded (ignore `node_modules`, logs); add a test
  asserting the scan completes fast on a synthetic tree.

### Slice 2.3 — `normalizeCapabilities` versions passthrough

- `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`: sanitize-and-preserve `versions.build`,
  `bootedAtMs`, `codeChangedSinceBoot` following the file's existing advisory-data rule
  (malformed → dropped, never a 400 — mirror `sanitizeDiscoveryStatus` bounds: capped
  strings, finite numbers, booleans).
- Old runners without `build` pass through unchanged (no `build` key, no error).
- Acceptance criterion 3 test lives here.

### Slice 2.4 — Release pipeline: bump enforcement (strict, per survey q5)

- New script (e.g. `scripts/check-runner-version-bump.mjs`): given a base ref (default: last
  release commit, same convention as `detect-changed-components.mjs`), fail (exit 1) when
  `runner/**` or `api/agent/harnesses/**` changed but `runner/version.json` `runnerVersion`
  did not increase (semver-greater than the base's copy).
- Wire into `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml` as an early gate step (before packaging),
  reusing `detect-changed-components.mjs` path semantics so the two cannot disagree on what
  "runner code" means.
- Edge cases: first release / missing base (warn, don't fail); pre-release tags (`-rc.N`)
  count as increases over the base; `version.json`-only releases pass trivially.
- Acceptance criterion 5 test: script-level tests with fixture git ranges (or a `--files`
  mode like `detect-changed-components.mjs --files` for hermetic tests) asserting
  fail-on-unbumped and pass-on-bumped.

### Slice 2.5 — Settings runner card: build sha + warning

- `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`: `describeRunnerBuild` (short sha,
  dirty marker, built-at) + `runnerBuildWarning(runner, backendSha)` predicate implementing
  survey q1–q4: warn on known sha mismatch or `codeChangedSinceBoot`, suppress warnings for
  dev runners (Spike 0.4 discriminator), never block.
- `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` (roster row + detail panel, exact card TBD by Spike 0.2):
  show short sha next to the existing version badge; render a warning banner inline on mismatch
  / changed-since-boot. Old runners (no `build`) show "unknown", no warning.
- Copy must say what to do ("restart or update this runner") without ever disabling actions —
  q15 warn-never-block.
- Acceptance criterion 4 test: component test asserting the warning renders for a mismatched
  fixture and stays hidden for matching/unknown fixtures.

## 8. Phase 3 — Assurance plan

### 8.1 Acceptance tests (one per criterion, must fail before / pass after)

| # | Test | Location | Fails today because |
|---|------|----------|---------------------|
| 1 | `factsFor()` output includes `versions.build.{sha,builtAt,dirty}` + `bootedAtMs` | `runner/daemon.test.js` | `versions` is only `{protocol,runner,api}` |
| 2 | touch a file in temp-dir fixture → next `factsFor()` reports `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` | `runner/daemon.test.js` (fixture from Phase 1.3) | field does not exist |
| 3 | `normalizeCapabilities` preserves `versions.build` (and drops malformed advisory values without errors) | dispatch test file for `normalizeCapabilities` | passthrough not implemented (currently raw passthrough — test pins the sanitized shape) |
| 4 | warning renders on sha mismatch / `codeChangedSinceBoot`; hidden on match/unknown/dev | `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` + helpers test | no build UI exists |
| 5 | bump-check script exits 1 on runner-code-change without version increase; 0 otherwise | new script test (hermetic `--files` mode) | script does not exist |

### 8.2 Regression gates (must stay green throughout)

- Runner update-channel gate (exact list from `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml`):
  `node --test runner/updates-*.test.js runner/config.test.js runner/daemon.test.js`.
- Full unit suites: `npm run test:unit` (api + frontend).
- Compat gate: `node scripts/check-component-compat.mjs` (version.json schema change must not
  break it — `build` is additive).
- Old-runner interop: heartbeat fixtures without `build` still normalize and render (covered
  by slices 2.3/2.5 negative tests). Old-backend interop: new `versions` keys are ignored, not
  rejected (verify against the backend's heartbeat validation tests).

### 8.3 Manual / visual verification

- Settings card: use the headless screenshot tool (`npm run capture:screenshot`) against a
  fixture runner in each state (match / mismatch / changed-since-boot / unknown / dev) —
  do not spawn long-lived background servers; use existing mock fixtures or the headless
  runner. Eyeball the warning copy and layout per Testing & Verification Guidance.
- End-to-end heartbeat check (optional, if a sandbox runner exists): boot a dev runner from
  the checkout, confirm `build.sha` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`, touch `runner/daemon.js`,
  confirm the next heartbeat carries `codeChangedSinceBoot: true`.

### 8.4 Documentation updates

- `runner/README.md` (or the runner docs page): document `build` fields, dev-checkout fallback,
  and what `codeChangedSinceBoot` means.
- Release docs (`docs/PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md` "Runner updates" section, referenced by the
  release workflow notes): document the bump requirement and the CI failure message + fix
  (bump `runnerVersion`).
- Settings/help copy if the UI has inline help for the Runners screen.
- This task folder: record Spike 0.1–0.5 outcomes (short notes) so WP-F and reviewers can
  follow the decisions.

### 8.5 Coordination and sequencing

- No blockers to start (spikes are self-contained).
- WP-B overlap (`runner/daemon.js`): keep slices 2.1/2.2 clear of `refreshDiscoveredModels`
  and boot sequencing; whoever merges second rebases. Prefer landing the Phase-1 extraction
  first so both work packages share the seam.
- Blocks WP-F: handoff is the shipped `versions.build` / `codeChangedSinceBoot` contract
  (field names, types, fallback semantics) — publish it in the PR description and link from
  this folder.

## 9. Risks and mitigations

- **Backend persistence gap** (Spike 0.2 outcome): if the runner record cannot carry `build`
  without backend changes outside the owned files, escalate scope before Slice 2.3 — do not
  smuggle backend edits into this work package.
- **Mtime-scan cost on every heartbeat**: bound the walk (single pass, skip heavy dirs,
  short-circuit once flipped); cover with a perf assertion test.
- **False positives**: clock skew / reinstalls flipping `codeChangedSinceBoot` — mitigate by
  comparing against boot fingerprint rather than wall-clock alone, and keep it warn-only so a
  false positive is cosmetic, never operational.
- **`git` unavailable in production bundles**: dev fallback must fail soft (`sha: null`);
  packaged runners always carry the stamp — CI test asserts the packaged archive contains a
  non-null `build.sha`.
- **Strict bump gate breaking hotfix flow**: gate fails only when runner-code paths changed
  without a version increase; provide a documented override (e.g. explicit label/env) only if
  the team asks — default is strict per survey q5.

## 10. Non-goals

- Auto-restart or restart button on stale detection (survey q3 follow-up).
- Dashboard banners or per-task warnings (survey q2 decided: card only).
- Blocking stale runners (forbidden by q15 except true incompatibility, which already exists).
- Changing `runner/updates` selection logic beyond making version data available.
- WP-B scope (`refreshDiscoveredModels`, boot sequencing, model discovery).

## 11. Open questions

1. SURVEY.md q1–q5 are unanswered — are the Recommended defaults adopted in §3 acceptable?
   (Assumption: yes; confirm before Slice 2.4/2.5.)
2. Where does the authoritative "backend sha" live? (Spike 0.3.)
3. What distinguishes a managed runner from a dev runner for q4 warning suppression?
   (Spike 0.4.)
4. Should the checked-in `runner/version.json` carry null `build` fields or omit `build`
   until stamped? (Decide in Slice 2.1; keep `check-component-compat` green either way.)
5. Does the update manifest need the build sha, or is semver comparison sufficient once bumps
   are enforced? (Slice 2.1 optional item.)

## 12. Work-order summary (earliest first)

1. Spikes 0.1–0.5 (research; unblock design decisions).
2. Phase 1 seams + characterization tests (safe refactors).
3. Slice 2.1 build identity + packager stamping.
4. Slice 2.2 heartbeat signal.
5. Slice 2.3 capabilities passthrough.
6. Slice 2.4 CI bump gate.
7. Slice 2.5 Settings card.
8. Phase 3 assurance (acceptance matrix, regression, screenshots, docs, WP-B rebase, WP-F handoff).

# Spike outcomes — WP-A build identity (task ae1ae677)

Short notes for reviewers and WP-F. All five Phase-0 spikes resolved during implementation.

## 0.1 — Which version.json does an installed runner read?

The booted daemon reads `runner/version.json` **beside itself** (`new URL("./version.json",
import.meta.url)` in `runner/daemon.js`). Installed layout is
`releases/<v>/unpacked/{runner/,api/,shared/,version.json}`, so the daemon reads
`unpacked/runner/version.json` — the **copied, unstamped** file. `scripts/package-runner.mjs`
only stamped the archive-root copy (`unpacked/version.json`, read by the updater's version
check and the wrapper doctor). Every self-updated Runner therefore kept reporting its old
`runnerVersion` (and now would have reported no build). Fix shipped: the packager stamps
**both** copies (pinned by `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs` through the real
`applyUpdate` staging path).

## 0.2 — How do versions reach the Settings card?

No backend persistence change needed. `RunnerRegistry._public` embeds the raw heartbeat
`facts` object verbatim in `GET /runners` records, so `facts.versions.build`,
`facts.versions.bootedAtMs`, and `facts.versions.codeChangedSinceBoot` flow to the
frontend untouched; `capabilities.versions` (via `normalizeCapabilities`, now
sanitize-and-preserve) carries the same block. The card reads
`capabilities.versions ?? facts.versions` (same fallback order as the discovery-status
summary). No backend files touched — owned-files list honoured.

## 0.3 — What is "backend sha"?

# Portable Deployment Guide

Cold-start KainBain on a machine that has never seen it — no homelab
services, no uncommitted notes, no author on call. Pick one scenario:

| | Scenario | Time | You get |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | [5-minute Docker](#scenario-a-5-minute-docker) | ~5 min | Production-shaped instance in containers |
| **B** | [Native dev](#scenario-b-native-dev-macoswindowslinux) | ~15 min | API + hot-reload frontend from source |
| **C** | [Work / corporate laptop](#scenario-c-workcorporate-laptop) | varies | Scenario A or B behind a proxy / custom CA / offline fonts |

Prerequisites for every scenario: `git`, and for Scenario A a working
Docker (`docker info` answers); for B/C, Node.js **≥ 20.19**
(`node --version` — the `engines` floor `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`;
`.nvmrc` pins 24 for development).

Every scenario ends with the [storage-sanity checklist](#storage-sanity-checklist).
Do not skip it: it is the tripwire for the 2026-10-02 incident class, where a
missing storage link silently degraded into a one-task shadow directory and the
UI showed 1 of 134 tasks. A future storage regression must fail the checklist,
never present an empty board.

> **Clone URL.** The canonical remote is GitHub at
> `https://github.com/Ewrdad/Kainbain.git`. If you are reading
> this in a private mirror, substitute that mirror's URL in the `git clone`
> line — everything after the clone is identical.

## Scenario A — 5-minute Docker

Production-shaped, self-contained, no credentials needed (harness calls
degrade honestly until you provide keys).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Ewrdad/Kainbain.git
cd KainBain
docker compose up -d
curl http://localhost:3100/status
```

Open **http://localhost:3100** — the frontend serves the built UI and proxies
the API from the same port, so there is only one URL.

What just happened: compose builds **two images from this checkout in one
`docker compose up --build`** (`backend` from `Dockerfile`, `frontend` from
`frontend/Dockerfile`, frontend compiled with same-origin API URLs). They
are independently versioned by API contract (see
`api/version.json`, `frontend/version.json`, `runner/version.json`): a
frontend may run against any backend inside its declared API range, and an
out-of-range pair shows an explicit UI banner naming both versions instead
of failing obscurely. The backend entrypoint verifies the task-storage mounts
*refuse-to-boot* style (an unreachable or unwritable projects root exits 1
rather than serving an empty list), and compose mounts `./projects` (your
tasks, on the host, survive rebuilds) plus a named volume for container
state. See [State ownership across the container boundary](#state-ownership-across-the-container-boundary) for which side writes what.

Useful follow-ups (all optional):

```bash
docker compose logs -f            # watch the boot log
KAINBAIN_PORT=3200 docker compose up -d   # move the host port on clash
cp .env.example .env              # then fill in ONLY secrets (API keys,
                                  # Ollama/LiteLLM URLs) — container paths
                                  # always win over .env
docker compose down               # stop (tasks stay in ./projects)
```

To enable real agent runs, set `KAINBAIN_DEFAULT_HARNESS=mock` in `.env`
for zero-credential evaluation, or add provider keys / a LiteLLM URL
(see [Scenario C](#scenario-c-workcorporate-laptop)) and recreate
(`docker compose up -d` again).

Publishing and deploying are separate steps. `./publish.sh` (repo root)
builds and pushes the changed components' images to Docker Hub and writes
`dist/release-manifest.json`; it never restarts anything.
`~/apps/kainbain/redeploy.sh` then pulls and restarts per component
(`--backend`, `--frontend`, `--runner`, `--all`; `--tag <tag>` pins a
previous tag for rollback). Set `KAINBAIN_DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE` wherever
publish runs. The pipeline's Publish stage runs `./publish.sh --detect`
and publishes only — deployment stays a human, local act. The old
`./deploy.sh --prod` path is retired (it prints the pointer above).

If this instance runs its own KainBain pipeline and deploys itself (a `ci`
stage whose command runs `./publish.sh --detect`, a host command that only
ever runs on the backend in the primary checkout), set `KAINBAIN_SELF_DEPLOY_CONTINUITY=1` in `.env`.
That implementation-specific flag enables the cross-restart continuity
plugin (`api/continuity/`) so the app survives its own redeploy; it is off
by default and generic projects never load that code.

Then run the [storage-sanity checklist](#storage-sanity-checklist).

## Scenario B — Native dev (macOS/Windows/Linux)

From-source dev: API on `:3100` with the Vite frontend on `:5173`.

**1. Install Node.js ≥ 20.19**, then verify:

```bash
node --version   # want v20.19.0 or newer (or v22.12.0+)
npm --version    # want 10 or newer
```

| OS | Install path |
|---|---|
| macOS | `brew install node@22`, or the LTS pkg from nodejs.org, or `nvm install 24` |
| Windows | The LTS `.msi` from nodejs.org, or `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` |
| Linux | The NodeSource distros, `nvm install 24`, or your package manager's ≥ 20.19 build |

(`.nvmrc` / `.node-version` pin 24 — `nvm use` just works. CI proves the
20.x floor and 22.x on all three OSs on every push.)

**2. Clone and install** (one command installs root + api + frontend +
canary trees, then Playwright Chromium — Linux additionally tries the
browser system deps and falls back with a warning without root):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Ewrdad/Kainbain.git
cd KainBain
npm run setup
```

**3. Configure (optional — defaults boot clean).** No `.env` is needed to
start: every knob has a default. When you need secrets or non-defaults:

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # fill in ONLY what you change; it is gitignored
```

Note the API does **not** auto-load `.env` — either export what you need
(`export KAINBAIN_DEFAULT_HARNESS=mock`) or start the API as
`node --env-file=.env api/index.js` (from the repo root). Every knob the
API reads is declared once in `api/config/schema.js`, validated at boot
(a malformed value fails the boot with a `CONFIG <VAR>: …` diagnostic —
fix the value), and documented in the generated `.env.example`.

If your API is not on `:3100`, tell the frontend where it lives (Vite
inlines these at dev start):

```bash
cp frontend/.env.example frontend/.env   # then set VITE_API_BASE / VITE_WS_URL
```

**4. Start both servers:**

```bash
npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` frees `:3100`/`:5173` (override with `PORT` / `VITE_PORT`),
then supervises the API (`node index.js` in `api/`) and Vite together —
Ctrl-C stops both. Prefer separate terminals:

```bash
(cd api && PORT=3100 node index.js)
(cd frontend && npm run dev)
```

Open **http://localhost:5173** (dev UI) — it talks to the API on `:3100`.

Then run the [storage-sanity checklist](#storage-sanity-checklist).

## Scenario C — Work/corporate laptop

Start from Scenario A (Docker) or B (native), then apply the corporate
adjustments you need. Each is independent.

**Proxy.** Install-time tooling honors the standard variables — set them
before `npm run setup` / `docker compose`:

```bash
export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080 HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080
export NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1
```

(`npm`, `git`, and Docker all read these; `NO_PROXY` keeps the local API,
Vite, and any same-machine LiteLLM direct.) Known gap, stated plainly:
the API's own outbound model calls do not currently route through
`HTTP_PROXY` — in a proxy-only network, point the box at an in-network
[local LiteLLM](#local-litellm-or-mock-harness) or run the
[mock harness](#local-litellm-or-mock-harness) instead of reaching clouds
directly.

**Custom CA.** Corporate TLS interception works with one variable — Node
honors it natively, and the server reads no other CA path, so boxes
without the homelab CA boot identically:

```bash
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/corp-ca.pem
```

Set it before `npm run setup` (npm/fetch trust) and before `npm run dev`
/ `docker compose up` (API trust). There is no implicit fallback: unset
means the OS default store only.

**Offline / blocked fonts.** The UI hard-links Google Fonts
(`fonts.googleapis.com` / `fonts.gstatic.com`) but loads them
asynchronously with system fallbacks (`Hanken Grotesk` →
`ui-sans-serif, system-ui`; `JetBrains Mono` → `ui-monospace, Menlo,
Consolas, monospace`): on a blocked network the app is fully usable in
fallback fonts, icon glyphs may show as text until the font arrives, and
nothing hangs waiting. No configuration needed.

**Git author.** Fresh machines often have no git identity — engine commits
would fail. Either set yours:

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "[REDACTED EMAIL]"
```

or do nothing: the API provisions a repo-local fallback
(`KAINBAIN_GIT_AUTHOR_NAME` / `KAINBAIN_GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`, defaulting to
`KainBain Agent <kainbain@local>`) the first time a project needs to
commit, never touching your global config.

**Local LiteLLM or mock harness.** Real agent runs need a model path —
pick one:

```bash
# Option 1: local LiteLLM (same machine or in-network; no cloud egress).
# The health probe tries, in order: LITELLM_URL, LITELLM_HOST,
# https://litellm.local, http://localhost:4000.
export LITELLM_URL=http://localhost:4000

# Option 2: zero-credential evaluation — deterministic echo sessions,
# no CLIs, no keys, no network. Explicit selection only; it never
# engages silently, so synthetic output can't mask a real outage.
export KAINBAIN_DEFAULT_HARNESS=mock
```

(Ollama Cloud follows the same shape: `OLLAMA_CLOUD_URL`, else
`https://ollama.com`, else `https://ollama.ai`. All three are optional —
unset means "not configured", honestly reported in health.)

Then run the [storage-sanity checklist](#storage-sanity-checklist).

## Scenario D — bring your existing repositories (multi-project)

Start from Scenario A (Docker) or B (native). This scenario points KainBain at
repositories you already have, across one or more directories, and optionally
gives a project its own state-folder name.

**1. Point at the roots that hold your repos.** `PROJECTS_ROOT` is the primary
root (one project per direct child directory); `PROJECTS_ROOTS` adds more.
Projects must be direct children of a root, or adopted explicitly (step 3).

```bash
# Linux/macOS (os path-list separator is ':'):
export PROJECTS_ROOT="$HOME/projects"
export PROJECTS_ROOTS="$HOME/work:/mnt/nas/repos"
# Windows (separator is ';'):
# set PROJECTS_ROOTS=%USERPROFILE%\work;D:\repos
```

Restart the API. Every direct child carrying a KainBain config file
(`<dir>/.kainbain/project.json`, or the project's custom state folder) appears
on the board. Stray directories are ignored, never turned into projects.

**2. Adopt a repo that lives outside every root.** Use the UI (**Project menu →
“+ Add Existing Project…”**) or the API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3100/projects/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"path":"/home/[REDACTED]/repos/one-off","name":"One Off","kainbainDirName":".kb"}'
```

Adopted directories outside every root are recorded in
`~/.kainbain/projects.json` (`KAINBAIN_PROJECTS_REGISTRY_FILE`) and re-discovered
after a restart. The call is idempotent. Repos inside a configured root need no
registry entry.

**3. Custom state folder (optional).** A project whose repo already owns
`.kainbain`, or that wants `.kb`, sets its state-folder name in **Project
Settings → KainBain Folder Name** (or `kainbainDirName` on the register/create
payload). Existing state is never moved automatically. Preferred flow: stop
the API, rename the folder, restart — the config is self-describing, so the
project re-scans from the new name with its state intact:

```bash
# stop the API first
cd /home/[REDACTED]/repos/one-off
mv .kainbain .kb   # only if you already had state under .kainbain
# start the API again
```

Changing the setting in the UI writes the new config and removes the superseded
one (a restart can never revert the setting or split state across two folders),
but `sessions/`, `worktrees/`, and `quarantine/` stay in the old folder — move
them across by hand.

Then run the [storage-sanity checklist](#storage-sanity-checklist).

## Storage-sanity checklist

Run this after every scenario, and again after any restore, migration, or
unclean shutdown. It takes two minutes and is the tripwire for the
empty-board incident class.

**1. The server answers.**

```bash
curl http://localhost:3100/status
```

Want: HTTP 200 with `"status":"ok"` JSON (Docker serves UI + API on
`:3100`; native dev serves the API on `:3100` and the UI on `:5173` —
use your `PORT` if you overrode it).

**2. The board is non-empty after a restore.** Create a project and a task
(substitute your port), restart the server, and count — the count must
survive the restart:

```bash
PID=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3100/projects \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Sanity"}' | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>s+=c).on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(s).id))")
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3100/tasks \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"projectId\":\"$PID\",\"title\":\"sanity\",\"goal\":\"prove restore\"}" > /dev/null
# ... restart the server (Ctrl-C + npm run dev, or docker compose restart) ...
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/tasks?projectId=$PID" \
  | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>s+=c).on('end',()=>console.log('task count after restart:',JSON.parse(s).length))"
```

Want: `task count after restart: 1` (or your pre-restart count — the
invariant is *unchanged and non-zero*, never silently zero).

**3. The automated form passes.** From the repo root:

```bash
node scripts/storage-sanity.mjs
```

Want: `storage-sanity: PASS (restore non-empty, shadow detector armed)`.
It boots fixture storage through the same `ensureDocsLink` + `scanTasks`
path the UI reads, asserts a 3-task restore is complete, and proves the
shadow detector fires. This is also a CI step on all six matrix legs.

**4. Know the diagnostic.** If the count ever drops unexpectedly, the
storage link is the first suspect. `ProjectStore.ensureDocsLink` reports
one state per project at startup (and `deploy.sh check_docs_link` echoes
the same warning on the deploy path):

| State | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | Link points at the configured notes space | none |
| `repaired` / `repaired-broken-link` | Missing/dangling link recreated | none (self-healed; in the log) |
| `shadowed` | Real `docs/` dir hides a populated notes space — the incident shape | **Stop.** Merge newer files from `docs/tasks/` into the notes space, then replace `docs` with a symlink to it. Never delete either side blind. |
| `foreign-link` | Link points at a different existing space | Point it at the configured notes space, or fix the config |
| `link-missing` / `broken-link` | Repair was attempted and failed (permissions?) | Fix the filesystem permission, restart |
| `notes-missing` | No notes space at all (fresh clone) | none on first boot; on an old box, restore the space |
| `local-dir` | Real dir, empty notes space (future local backend) | none |
| `no-cwd` | Project record has no working directory (corrupt `project.json`) | Fix or re-create the project record |
| `unexpected` | `docs` is neither a symlink nor a directory | Inspect it by hand; then re-run this checklist |

The `shadowed` log line quotes the merge procedure verbatim — follow it,
then re-run this checklist.

**5. A fresh boot has no junk projects.** On a clean machine the board starts
empty: sample projects (`Project A`–`Project D`) are **not** seeded unless you
set `KAINBAIN_SEED_SAMPLE_PROJECTS=1`. If you see them, the flag is on or they
are genuinely on disk from an older run — remove the directories under
`PROJECTS_ROOT`, or hide them with the project switcher’s *Hide* action.

**6. Every configured root is discovered.** Adopt a repo outside every root
(`POST /projects/register`), restart, and confirm it is still on the board:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3100/projects \
  | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>s+=c).on('end',()=>{
      const p=JSON.parse(s).map(x=>x.cwd).sort();console.log(p.join('\\n'));})"
```

Want: every root’s projects plus the adopted path. A missing adopted project
means the registry file (`~/.kainbain/projects.json`) is unreadable — check
permissions and re-run the register call.

## State ownership across the container boundary

The one place that says which side writes what (D10, MigrationPlan Phase 1
WP-1.2). The invariant underneath is unchanged: the repo/filesystem is the
source of truth for projects and tasks; nothing here adds a database.

| Mount | Held by | Contents | Writers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `./projects` → `/workspace/projects` | backend | Master project copies — repo-as-truth (project configs, `docs/tasks/` run state) | **Backend only.** The only writer of project/task files. |
| `kainbain-data` → `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` | backend | Container state: notes space, sessions, caches, `build.json` stamp | **Backend only** (entrypoint verifies writability at boot; an unreachable mount is a fatal boot error, never a silent empty board). |
| (none) | frontend | Nothing at runtime — static UI + proxy config, `VITE_*` baked at build | No writes possible. A stale frontend can only disagree by version, which the mismatch banner names. |
| Runner working dirs (Phase 2+) | each Runner (native, outside compose) | Git-operation copies: per-task worktrees | Runners mutate **only** their own worktree and push their branch; they converge via push + completion report. No second writable store for task truth exists — adding one is the programme kill criterion. |

Consequences for operators:

- General config (schema-driven settings plus `.env` secrets) is read by the
  backend from its mounted folder; the frontend takes configuration only as
  build-time `VITE_*` args. A frontend container never needs a volume.
- `docker compose down` loses nothing: tasks live in `./projects` on the
  host, state in the named volume. `docker compose down -v` discards the
  named volume (sessions, caches) but never `./projects`.
- Rollback to the single-service topology is `git show
  HEAD~:docker-compose.yml` (or any pre-split commit): the backend image
  still ships `frontend/dist` and serves it when reached directly.
- New projects will require a fetchable remote (decided, D11); enforcement
  lands with the Runner work. Existing local-only projects keep the
  loopback transport and are never offered to remote Runners.

## Runner updates (external artifact channel, ADR 0012)

External Runners self-update from versioned GitHub Releases — never from
the backend (rejected Option B: backend-served code would maximise the R05
blast radius and couple updates to backend uptime).

- **Automatic, idle-only, compatibility-gated.** The dispatch loop checks
  `https://api.github.com/repos/Ewrdad/Kainbain/releases/latest` on a
  jittered hourly interval (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`,
  min 5 min) when it holds no task, and immediately (interval bypassed)
  when the backend refuses dispatch with 409
  `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM`. It installs the newest release that is
  strictly newer, not a pre-release, and compatible with the backend it
  talks to (each manifest's `requires.backendApi` range must admit the
  backend API version learned from heartbeats) — never "latest,
  always". When latest verifies but is incompatible, the GitHub path
  walks one bounded releases-list page (30 entries, newest-first) for
  the newest older release that qualifies. Set
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` to opt out. Pointer/manifest fetches
  time out after 30s, asset downloads after 5 min — a hung mirror backs
  off and retries instead of wedging the loop, and any failure keeps
  the old version running.
- **Verified, not trusted.** The manifest signature is checked against the
  public key pinned in `runner/updates/verify.js` (never fetched from the
  network), then the asset sha256 against the manifest. Any mismatch aborts,
  keeps the old version running, and reports via heartbeat facts
  (`updateStatus`) for the Settings › Runners "update failed" badge.
- **Atomic with rollback.** The new tree stages under
  `$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/releases/<v>/unpacked`, then the
  `current` symlink flips (previous kept as `previous`). The daemon exits 0
  and `runner/bin/kainbain-runner` (the supported entrypoint) restarts it
  into the new version — the wrapper only restarts when the `current`
  target actually changed during the run, so a normal completion (single
  assignment done, dispatch idle-out) stops instead of re-running finished
  work. Three crashed boots in a row flip `current` back to
  `previous` automatically. Direct `node runner/main.js` is dev-only after
  the first update — it cannot restart itself. A stale `update.lock` from
  a crashed updater heals itself (dead holder is detected and the lock
  recycled, so one crash never bricks future updates), and the first
  successful heartbeat on the new version prunes superseded releases while
  always keeping `current` + `previous`.
- **Backend coordination, no code transfer.** Runners report
  `facts.versions.runner` on register/heartbeat, and the backend
  advertises its update directive back (`backendApiVersion`,
  `desiredRunnerVersion`, `minimumRunnerVersion` inside the `update`
  object). Settings › Runners shows the fleet version matrix with an
  "update available" badge (below `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION`)
  and a "below minimum" flag. Dispatch and direct claim refuse Runners
  below `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` with 409 (routine releases raise
  only the recommended knob, so dispatch keeps flowing). The backend
  also auto-commands updates: heartbeats queue `requestUpdate` for
  active, command-capable Runners trailing the recommended version (at
  most daily per Runner); Runners still apply only when idle. Desired
  nudges, never caps — a Runner may run newer than desired while
  backend-compatible.
- **Rollback a bad release.** Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release
  so `releases/latest` resolves to the prior tag, then lower
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to stop badge nagging. Runners still
  on older versions pick the prior release up on their next idle check.
  Runners already on the bad release stay there until a newer release
  supersedes it — the updater never downgrades — so cut a patch release to
  move them forward. Two exceptions: a release that crashes on boot rolls
  itself back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` above the bad version stops it dispatching
  (409) while the patch is cut. Re-tagging is never needed.
- **Bump the version with every runner-code release.** The self-updater
  compares versions, not bytes, so a release that changes `runner/**` or
  `api/agent/harnesses/**` without increasing `runnerVersion` would ship
  code no Runner is ever offered. The `version-bump-gate` job in
  `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml` (via
  `scripts/check-runner-version-bump.mjs`) fails such a release before any
  archive is built. Fix: bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json`
  and re-tag (test/spec files, markdown docs, and the version file itself
  never trigger the gate). The normal flow needs no manual tagging:
  bump, merge, and `./publish.sh --runner` cuts `runner-v*` from the
  bumped version.
- **Air-gapped/offline hosts.** Point `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_UPDATE_URL` at a
  mirror serving `manifest.json` + `manifest.json.minisig` + the asset
  tarballs at one base URL (or a full `manifest.json` URL). The same
  signature + sha256 gates apply to mirrors. A mirror base may also
  serve a `releases.json` index (`{ schema: 1, component: "runner",
  releases: [{ version, manifestUrl, signatureUrl }] }`, newest-first)
  so compat-gated selection can walk older releases exactly like the
  GitHub path; a missing index (404) falls back to the single manifest,
  while a present-but-invalid index fails the check loudly. Hosts that
  can only reach the backend (not GitHub) update through such a mirror
  on their own network — the backend itself never serves bytes (R05).
- **First-release key provisioning (operator, once).** Run
  `node scripts/runner-release-keygen.mjs`, commit the printed public line
  to `scripts/runner-pinned-key/runner-release.pub` **and** to
  `PINNED_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY` in `runner/updates/verify.js` (CI fails the
  release when they differ), and store the secret halves in the GitHub
  Actions secrets `RUNNER_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY` / `RUNNER_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEYNUM`.
  Cutting a release is: bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json`,
  merge, and publish the runner (`publish.sh` cuts and pushes the
  annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which triggers the release builder);
  manual `git tag runner-vX.Y.Z && git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z` stays
  the emergency path (pre-release tags `*-rc.N`/`*-beta*`/`*-alpha*`
  publish as pre-release and are skipped by v1 Runners; the manifest
  keeps the full canary version, never the stripped final it previews).
  Full procedure, rollback drill, wrapper migration, and "says out of
  date" triage live in `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`. `minisign` CLI install is not required
  anywhere — signing and verification are pure Node + Ed25519. Linux and
  macOS (x64/arm64) ship; Windows is deferred.
- **Linux/macOS only in v1** (x64 + arm64, four assets per release).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` says a port is taken | `PORT=3210 VITE_PORT=5210 npm run dev` (and point `frontend/.env` at the API port) |
| `docker compose up` port clash | `KAINBAIN_PORT=3200 docker compose up -d` |
| `engines` / `EBADENGINE` on install | Upgrade Node to ≥ 20.19 on the 20.x line, or ≥ 22.12 (`node --version`) |
| Playwright system-deps warning on Linux | Harmless without root — the browser installs alone; install OS packages only if Chromium fails to launch |
| `CONFIG <VAR>: …` boot failure | The named variable is malformed — fix its value (missing/empty still falls back to the default silently) |
| Windows symlink privilege error | Enable Developer Mode (or run elevated once) — project creation symlinks `docs/`; the failure is loud, never silent |
| Board shows fewer tasks than expected | Storage-sanity checklist step 4 — check for `shadowed` before anything else |

## What this guide does not cover

The author's homelab production deployment (systemd user unit, nginx,
`https://kainbain.home`) is documented in the root `README.md` under
"Author's homelab production setup" — it is one specific production
instance, not a procedure. Everything above stands without it.
