## Scenario A — 5-minute Docker

Production-shaped, self-contained, no credentials needed (harness calls
degrade honestly until you provide keys).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Ewrdad/Kainbain.git
cd KainBain
docker compose up -d
curl http://localhost:3100/status
```

Open **http://localhost:3100** — the frontend serves the built UI and proxies
the API from the same port, so there is only one URL.

What just happened: compose builds **two images from this checkout in one
`docker compose up --build`** (`backend` from `Dockerfile`, `frontend` from
`frontend/Dockerfile`, frontend compiled with same-origin API URLs). They
are independently versioned by API contract (see
`api/version.json`, `frontend/version.json`, `runner/version.json`): a
frontend may run against any backend inside its declared API range, and an
out-of-range pair shows an explicit UI banner naming both versions instead
of failing obscurely. The backend entrypoint verifies the task-storage mounts
*refuse-to-boot* style (an unreachable or unwritable projects root exits 1
rather than serving an empty list), and compose mounts `./projects` (your
tasks, on the host, survive rebuilds) plus a named volume for container
state. See [State ownership across the container boundary](#state-ownership-across-the-container-boundary) for which side writes what.

Useful follow-ups (all optional):

```bash
docker compose logs -f            # watch the boot log
KAINBAIN_PORT=3200 docker compose up -d   # move the host port on clash
cp .env.example .env              # then fill in ONLY secrets (API keys,
                                  # Ollama/LiteLLM URLs) — container paths
                                  # always win over .env
docker compose down               # stop (tasks stay in ./projects)
```

To enable real agent runs, set `KAINBAIN_DEFAULT_HARNESS=mock` in `.env`
for zero-credential evaluation, or add provider keys / a LiteLLM URL
(see [Scenario C](#scenario-c-workcorporate-laptop)) and recreate
(`docker compose up -d` again).

Publishing and deploying are separate steps. `./publish.sh` (repo root)
builds and pushes the changed components' images to Docker Hub and writes
`dist/release-manifest.json`; it never restarts anything.
`~/apps/kainbain/redeploy.sh` then pulls and restarts per component
(`--backend`, `--frontend`, `--runner`, `--all`; `--tag <tag>` pins a
previous tag for rollback). Set `KAINBAIN_DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE` wherever
publish runs. The pipeline's Publish stage runs `./publish.sh --detect`
and publishes only — deployment stays a human, local act. The old
`./deploy.sh --prod` path is retired (it prints the pointer above).

If this instance runs its own KainBain pipeline and deploys itself (a `ci`
stage whose command runs `./publish.sh --detect`, a host command that only
ever runs on the backend in the primary checkout), set `KAINBAIN_SELF_DEPLOY_CONTINUITY=1` in `.env`.
That implementation-specific flag enables the cross-restart continuity
plugin (`api/continuity/`) so the app survives its own redeploy; it is off
by default and generic projects never load that code.

Then run the [storage-sanity checklist](#storage-sanity-checklist).

## Scenario B — Native dev (macOS/Windows/Linux)

From-source dev: API on `:3100` with the Vite frontend on `:5173`.

**1. Install Node.js ≥ 20.19**, then verify:

```bash
node --version   # want v20.19.0 or newer (or v22.12.0+)
npm --version    # want 10 or newer
```

| OS | Install path |
|---|---|
| macOS | `brew install node@22`, or the LTS pkg from nodejs.org, or `nvm install 24` |
| Windows | The LTS `.msi` from nodejs.org, or `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` |
| Linux | The NodeSource distros, `nvm install 24`, or your package manager's ≥ 20.19 build |

(`.nvmrc` / `.node-version` pin 24 — `nvm use` just works. CI proves the
20.x floor and 22.x on all three OSs on every push.)

**2. Clone and install** (one command installs root + api + frontend +
canary trees, then Playwright Chromium — Linux additionally tries the
browser system deps and falls back with a warning without root):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Ewrdad/Kainbain.git
cd KainBain
npm run setup
```

**3. Configure (optional — defaults boot clean).** No `.env` is needed to
start: every knob has a default. When you need secrets or non-defaults:

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # fill in ONLY what you change; it is gitignored
```

Note the API does **not** auto-load `.env` — either export what you need
(`export KAINBAIN_DEFAULT_HARNESS=mock`) or start the API as
`node --env-file=.env api/index.js` (from the repo root). Every knob the
API reads is declared once in `api/config/schema.js`, validated at boot
(a malformed value fails the boot with a `CONFIG <VAR>: …` diagnostic —
fix the value), and documented in the generated `.env.example`.

If your API is not on `:3100`, tell the frontend where it lives (Vite
inlines these at dev start):

```bash
cp frontend/.env.example frontend/.env   # then set VITE_API_BASE / VITE_WS_URL
```

**4. Start both servers:**

```bash
npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` frees `:3100`/`:5173` (override with `PORT` / `VITE_PORT`),
then supervises the API (`node index.js` in `api/`) and Vite together —
Ctrl-C stops both. Prefer separate terminals:

```bash
(cd api && PORT=3100 node index.js)
(cd frontend && npm run dev)
```

Open **http://localhost:5173** (dev UI) — it talks to the API on `:3100`.

Then run the [storage-sanity checklist](#storage-sanity-checklist).

## Scenario C — Work/corporate laptop

Start from Scenario A (Docker) or B (native), then apply the corporate
adjustments you need. Each is independent.

**Proxy.** Install-time tooling honors the standard variables — set them
before `npm run setup` / `docker compose`:

```bash
export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080 HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080
export NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1
```

(`npm`, `git`, and Docker all read these; `NO_PROXY` keeps the local API,
Vite, and any same-machine LiteLLM direct.) Known gap, stated plainly:
the API's own outbound model calls do not currently route through
`HTTP_PROXY` — in a proxy-only network, point the box at an in-network
[local LiteLLM](#local-litellm-or-mock-harness) or run the
[mock harness](#local-litellm-or-mock-harness) instead of reaching clouds
directly.

**Custom CA.** Corporate TLS interception works with one variable — Node

# Audit: Update Safety and Existing Installation Compatibility

**Task:** Give runners a build identity and stale-code detection (`ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084`)  
**Stage:** Update Safety Verification (Docs-Only)  
**Date:** 2026-11-14  

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We audited the changes implemented on branch `kb/ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084` to verify whether the build identity and stale-code detection features could break existing runner installations when they update or interact with the backend.

**Verdict: SAFE (PASS)**.
The implementation preserves backward and forward compatibility across all layers:
- Existing runner installations updating via `applyUpdate` receive valid bundles stamped with version and build identity without breaking file layout expectations.
- Unupdated (legacy) runners reporting to an updated backend are accepted without errors or schema rejections.
- Updated runners reporting to older backends send backwards-compatible additive fields that do not disrupt older parsers.
- Dev runners running directly from git checkouts and production runners packaged as tarballs operate without crashes, graceful degradation is implemented for all fallback paths, and version mismatch warnings never block execution.

---

## 2. Detailed Findings

### A. Packaging & Packaging Layout (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`)
- `packageRunner` writes `version.json` containing `runnerVersion` and `build` (`{ sha, builtAt, dirty }`) into **both** required locations:
  1. Staging root (`version.json`), read by the self-updater's version checker and wrapper doctor.
  2. Subdirectory (`runner/version.json`), read by the daemon at runtime (`new URL("./version.json", import.meta.url)`).
- Verified via `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`:
  - `a packaged bundle stages through the real applyUpdate`: Passes.
  - `stamps the release version and build into both version.json copies`: Passes.
  - `a staged bundle's daemon-readable copy self-identifies as the release`: Passes.
- The bundle layout (`runner/`, `shared/`, `api/`, `version.json`, `INSTALL.txt`) is strictly preserved; runtime extras migration (`api/node_modules`) inside `applyUpdate` continues to operate cleanly.

### B. Daemon Boot & Stale-Code Detection (`runner/daemon.js`)
- `RUNNER_BUILD` resolution uses fallback resolution:
  - If stamped in `version.json` (packaged release), the stamp is used directly.
  - If running in a git checkout without a package stamp, it safely queries `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain`.
  - If git is absent or fails, it gracefully falls back to `{ sha: null, builtAt: null, dirty: null, source: null }` without throwing.
- Stale-code detection (`snapshotCodeTree` / `hasCodeChangedSinceBoot`) is strictly warn-only:
  - Missing directory, unreadable tree, or empty baseline returns `false` (no false positives, fails quiet).
  - Ignores `.git` and `node_modules` to avoid flagging harmless file updates.
  - Each heartbeat receives a defensive clone of `RUNNER_BUILD` (`build: { ...RUNNER_BUILD }`), preventing middleware mutations from corrupting module state.

### C. Backend Normalization & Protocol Compatibility (`api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`)
- `sanitizeVersions` handles all legacy and future shapes:
  - Legacy runners sending `{ protocol: 'v1', runner: '0.1.0' }` without `build` pass through untouched; `build` is not injected if absent.
  - `build`, `bootedAtMs`, and `codeChangedSinceBoot` are sanitized leniently.
  - Any unknown future keys in `facts.versions` pass through untouched.
  - Malformed version objects or invalid types degrade gracefully to null or are deleted rather than throwing a 400 rejection.
- Heartbeat registration and updates remain non-blocking.

### D. Settings UI & Survey Constraints (`frontend/src/components/settings/`)
- Adheres to Survey round-2 q15 constraint: version or build mismatch produces an advisory warning banner and **never blocks** task claims or runner execution.
- If `build` is absent (legacy runner), the UI renders standard version info without errors or crash loops.

### E. CI Version Bump Gate (`scripts/check-runner-version-bump.mjs`)
- Enforces version bumps on releases touching runner code while ignoring docs (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdx`) and test files (`.test.*`, `.spec.*`).
- Existing release workflows are not disrupted for non-runner changes.

---

## 3. Test Verification
All touched and related test suites pass:
- `runner/daemon.test.js` (build identity, factsFor, codeChangedSinceBoot)
- `runner/updates-*.test.js` (all 103 update check, verify, manifest, and apply tests pass)
- `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs` (all conformance and staging tests pass)
- `tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs` (gate logic tests pass)
- `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.test.js` (15/15 tests pass via vitest)
- Frontend unit tests: `runnerConfigHelpers.test.js` and `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` (111/111 tests pass via vitest)

1|# Audit: Update Safety and Existing Installation Compatibility
2|
3|**Task:** Give runners a build identity and stale-code detection (`ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084`)  
4|**Stage:** Update Safety Verification (Docs-Only)  
5|**Date:** 2026-11-14  
6|
7|---
8|
9|## 1. Executive Summary
10|
11|We audited the changes implemented on branch `kb/ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084` to verify whether the build identity and stale-code detection features could break existing runner installations when they update or interact with the backend.
12|
13|**Verdict: SAFE (PASS)**.
14|The implementation preserves backward and forward compatibility across all layers:
15|- Existing runner installations updating via `applyUpdate` receive valid bundles stamped with version and build identity without breaking file layout expectations.
16|- Unupdated (legacy) runners reporting to an updated backend are accepted without errors or schema rejections.
17|- Updated runners reporting to older backends send backwards-compatible additive fields that do not disrupt older parsers.
18|- Dev runners running directly from git checkouts and production runners packaged as tarballs operate without crashes, graceful degradation is implemented for all fallback paths, and version mismatch warnings never block execution.
19|
20|---
21|
22|## 2. Detailed Findings
23|
24|### A. Packaging & Packaging Layout (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`)
25|- `packageRunner` writes `version.json` containing `runnerVersion` and `build` (`{ sha, builtAt, dirty }`) into **both** required locations:
26|  1. Staging root (`version.json`), read by the self-updater's version checker and wrapper doctor.
27|  2. Subdirectory (`runner/version.json`), read by the daemon at runtime (`new URL("./version.json", import.meta.url)`).
28|- Verified via `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`:
29|  - `a packaged bundle stages through the real applyUpdate`: Passes.
30|  - `stamps the release version and build into both version.json copies`: Passes.
31|  - `a staged bundle's daemon-readable copy self-identifies as the release`: Passes.
32|- The bundle layout (`runner/`, `shared/`, `api/`, `version.json`, `INSTALL.txt`) is strictly preserved; runtime extras migration (`api/node_modules`) inside `applyUpdate` continues to operate cleanly.
33|
34|### B. Daemon Boot & Stale-Code Detection (`runner/daemon.js`)
35|- `RUNNER_BUILD` resolution uses fallback resolution:
36|  - If stamped in `version.json` (packaged release), the stamp is used directly.
37|  - If running in a git checkout without a package stamp, it safely queries `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain`.
38|  - If git is absent or fails, it gracefully falls back to `{ sha: null, builtAt: null, dirty: null, source: null }` without throwing.
39|- Stale-code detection (`snapshotCodeTree` / `hasCodeChangedSinceBoot`) is strictly warn-only:
40|  - Missing directory, unreadable tree, or empty baseline returns `false` (no false positives, fails quiet).
41|  - Ignores `.git` and `node_modules` to avoid flagging harmless file updates.
42|  - Each heartbeat receives a defensive clone of `RUNNER_BUILD` (`build: { ...RUNNER_BUILD }`), preventing middleware mutations from corrupting module state.
43|
44|### C. Backend Normalization & Protocol Compatibility (`api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`)
45|- `sanitizeVersions` handles all legacy and future shapes:
46|  - Legacy runners sending `{ protocol: 'v1', runner: '0.1.0' }` without `build` pass through untouched; `build` is not injected if absent.
47|  - `build`, `bootedAtMs`, and `codeChangedSinceBoot` are sanitized leniently.
48|  - Any unknown future keys in `facts.versions` pass through untouched.
49|  - Malformed version objects or invalid types degrade gracefully to null or are deleted rather than throwing a 400 rejection.
50|- Heartbeat registration and updates remain non-blocking.
51|
52|### D. Settings UI & Survey Constraints (`frontend/src/components/settings/`)
53|- Adheres to Survey round-2 q15 constraint: version or build mismatch produces an advisory warning banner and **never blocks** task claims or runner execution.
54|- If `build` is absent (legacy runner), the UI renders standard version info without errors or crash loops.
55|
56|### E. CI Version Bump Gate (`scripts/check-runner-version-bump.mjs`)
57|- Enforces version bumps on releases touching runner code while ignoring docs (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdx`) and test files (`.test.*`, `.spec.*`).
58|- Existing release workflows are not disrupted for non-runner changes.
59|
60|---
61|
62|## 3. Test Verification
63|All touched and related test suites pass:
64|- `runner/daemon.test.js` (build identity, factsFor, codeChangedSinceBoot)
65|- `runner/updates-*.test.js` (all 103 update check, verify, manifest, and apply tests pass)
66|- `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs` (all conformance and staging tests pass)
67|- `tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs` (gate logic tests pass)
68|- `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.test.js` (15/15 tests pass via vitest)
69|- Frontend unit tests: `runnerConfigHelpers.test.js` and `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` (111/111 tests pass via vitest)

1|# Audit: Update Safety and Existing Installation Compatibility
2|
3|**Task:** Give runners a build identity and stale-code detection (`ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084`)  
4|**Stage:** Update Safety Verification (Docs-Only)  
5|**Date:** 2026-11-14  
6|
7|---
8|
9|## 1. Executive Summary
10|
11|We audited the changes implemented on branch `kb/ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084` to verify whether the build identity and stale-code detection features could break existing runner installations when they update or interact with the backend.
12|
13|**Verdict: SAFE (PASS)**.
14|The implementation preserves backward and forward compatibility across all layers:
15|- Existing runner installations updating via `applyUpdate` receive valid bundles stamped with version and build identity without breaking file layout expectations.
16|- Unupdated (legacy) runners reporting to an updated backend are accepted without errors or schema rejections.
17|- Updated runners reporting to older backends send backwards-compatible additive fields that do not disrupt older parsers.
18|- Dev runners running directly from git checkouts and production runners packaged as tarballs operate without crashes, graceful degradation is implemented for all fallback paths, and version mismatch warnings never block execution.
19|
20|---
21|
22|## 2. Detailed Findings
23|
24|### A. Packaging & Packaging Layout (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`)
25|- `packageRunner` writes `version.json` containing `runnerVersion` and `build` (`{ sha, builtAt, dirty }`) into **both** required locations:
26|  1. Staging root (`version.json`), read by the self-updater's version checker and wrapper doctor.
27|  2. Subdirectory (`runner/version.json`), read by the daemon at runtime (`new URL("./version.json", import.meta.url)`).
28|- Verified via `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`:
29|  - `a packaged bundle stages through the real applyUpdate`: Passes.
30|  - `stamps the release version and build into both version.json copies`: Passes.
31|  - `a staged bundle's daemon-readable copy self-identifies as the release`: Passes.
32|- The bundle layout (`runner/`, `shared/`, `api/`, `version.json`, `INSTALL.txt`) is strictly preserved; runtime extras migration (`api/node_modules`) inside `applyUpdate` continues to operate cleanly.
33|
34|### B. Daemon Boot & Stale-Code Detection (`runner/daemon.js`)
35|- `RUNNER_BUILD` resolution uses fallback resolution:
36|  - If stamped in `version.json` (packaged release), the stamp is used directly.
37|  - If running in a git checkout without a package stamp, it safely queries `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain`.
38|  - If git is absent or fails, it gracefully falls back to `{ sha: null, builtAt: null, dirty: null, source: null }` without throwing.
39|- Stale-code detection (`snapshotCodeTree` / `hasCodeChangedSinceBoot`) is strictly warn-only:
40|  - Missing directory, unreadable tree, or empty baseline returns `false` (no false positives, fails quiet).
41|  - Ignores `.git` and `node_modules` to avoid flagging harmless file updates.
42|  - Each heartbeat receives a defensive clone of `RUNNER_BUILD` (`build: { ...RUNNER_BUILD }`), preventing middleware mutations from corrupting module state.
43|
44|### C. Backend Normalization & Protocol Compatibility (`api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`)
45|- `sanitizeVersions` handles all legacy and future shapes:
46|  - Legacy runners sending `{ protocol: 'v1', runner: '0.1.0' }` without `build` pass through untouched; `build` is not injected if absent.
47|  - `build`, `bootedAtMs`, and `codeChangedSinceBoot` are sanitized leniently.
48|  - Any unknown future keys in `facts.versions` pass through untouched.
49|  - Malformed version objects or invalid types degrade gracefully to null or are deleted rather than throwing a 400 rejection.
50|- Heartbeat registration and updates remain non-blocking.
51|
52|### D. Settings UI & Survey Constraints (`frontend/src/components/settings/`)
53|- Adheres to Survey round-2 q15 constraint: version or build mismatch produces an advisory warning banner and **never blocks** task claims or runner execution.
54|- If `build` is absent (legacy runner), the UI renders standard version info without errors or crash loops.
55|
56|### E. CI Version Bump Gate (`scripts/check-runner-version-bump.mjs`)
57|- Enforces version bumps on releases touching runner code while ignoring docs (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdx`) and test files (`.test.*`, `.spec.*`).
58|- Existing release workflows are not disrupted for non-runner changes.
59|

65|- `runner/updates-*.test.js` (all 103 update check, verify, manifest, and apply tests pass)

1|# Spike outcomes — WP-A build identity (task ae1ae677)
2|
3|Short notes for reviewers and WP-F. All five Phase-0 spikes resolved during implementation.
4|
5|## 0.1 — Which version.json does an installed runner read?
6|
7|The booted daemon reads `runner/version.json` **beside itself** (`new URL("./version.json",
8|import.meta.url)` in `runner/daemon.js`). Installed layout is
9|`releases/<v>/unpacked/{runner/,api/,shared/,version.json}`, so the daemon reads
10|`unpacked/runner/version.json` — the **copied, unstamped** file. `scripts/package-runner.mjs`
11|only stamped the archive-root copy (`unpacked/version.json`, read by the updater's version
12|check and the wrapper doctor). Every self-updated Runner therefore kept reporting its old
13|`runnerVersion` (and now would have reported no build). Fix shipped: the packager stamps
14|**both** copies (pinned by `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs` through the real
15|`applyUpdate` staging path).
16|
17|## 0.2 — How do versions reach the Settings card?
18|
19|No backend persistence change needed. `RunnerRegistry._public` embeds the raw heartbeat
20|`facts` object verbatim in `GET /runners` records, so `facts.versions.build`,
21|`facts.versions.bootedAtMs`, and `facts.versions.codeChangedSinceBoot` flow to the
22|frontend untouched; `capabilities.versions` (via `normalizeCapabilities`, now
23|sanitize-and-preserve) carries the same block. The card reads
24|`capabilities.versions ?? facts.versions` (same fallback order as the discovery-status
25|summary). No backend files touched — owned-files list honoured.
26|
27|## 0.3 — What is "backend sha"?
28|
29|`GET /status` → `build.commit` (from `deployManager.readBuild()`, already fetched by the
30|frontend's cached `api.systemStatus()`). Zero backend changes. Comparison is prefix-aware
31|(short backend commit vs full runner sha), case-insensitive, minimum 4 chars; unknown on
32|either side disables only the sha-mismatch branch, never the changed-since-boot branch.
33|
34|## 0.4 — Managed-vs-dev discriminator (survey q4)
35|
36|No existing signal, so the build itself carries one: new additive `build.source` —
37|`"package"` (release stamp) vs `"checkout"` (dev git fallback at boot) vs `null`
38|(unknown). The card shows build info for all runners but suppresses warnings for
39|`source === "checkout"`. No new registry invented.
40|
41|## 0.5 — Heartbeat test surface
42|
43|Seams shipped: `factsFor` exported with a `codeTree: { rootDir, baseline, bootedAtMs }`
44|override (temp-dir fixtures, no global mutation); pure `loadRunnerVersionInfo` /
45|`resolveRunnerBuild` / `snapshotCodeTree` / `hasCodeChangedSinceBoot` (node:test);
46|`normalizeCapabilities` passthrough (api vitest); `describeRunnerBuild` /
47|`runnerBuildWarning` (frontend vitest); bump gate with `--files` + `--root` hermetic
48|modes (tests/*.test.mjs in the Harness Self-Tests branch).
49|
50|## Shipped heartbeat contract (WP-F handoff)
51|
52|`facts.versions = { protocol, runner, api, build: { sha, builtAt, dirty, source },
53|bootedAtMs, codeChangedSinceBoot }`. Old runners omit the new keys (render "unknown",
54|no warning); old backends ignore them. Blocking behaviour unchanged
55|(`RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` only) — warn, never block.
56|
57|## Open questions closed
58|
59|- Q1–Q5/Q15 survey defaults: adopted as specified in the plan.
60|- Checked-in `runner/version.json`: carries explicit null `build` (self-documenting
61|  schema; `check-component-compat` unaffected — verified green).
62|- Manifest build sha (Q5): skipped — semver comparison is sufficient once bumps are
63|  enforced, and `runner/updates` selection changes are an explicit non-goal.
64|- `publish.sh` tag-skip path: left as-is (idempotent skip is pinned by
65|  `tests/publish.test.mjs`); enforcement lives in the release-workflow gate, which is
66|  where a mistagged release is actually stopped.

Read text file `docs/tasks/ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# Implementation Plan — Runner build identity and stale-code detection
2|
3|Task: `ae1ae677-7eb5-432c-b0d5-20c72e833084` · Parent bug: `b3401f19` · Source work package: WP-A (cause N1).
4|Blocks: WP-F. Shared-file coordination: WP-B also touches `runner/daemon.js` (only `refreshDiscoveredModels`/boot) — whichever merges second rebases.
5|
6|## 1. Goal
7|
8|Give every runner a verifiable build identity (`build { sha, builtAt, dirty }`) plus a boot-time
9|code hash and per-heartbeat stale-code signal (`codeChangedSinceBoot`, `bootedAtMs`), make the
10|release pipeline stamp and enforce version bumps so `runner/updates` can actually offer updates,
11|and surface a **warning (never a block)** in the Settings runner card when a runner is stale.
12|
13|Why: per RESPONSE.md N1, `runner/version.json` has said `0.1.0` since 2026-10-31, all runners
14|report `versions.runner 0.1.0`, the self-updater never fires, and past tickets "fixed" code that
15|runners never picked up. A runner whose files change after boot (e.g. `runner/daemon.js` mtime
16|4s after boot on local-bravo) is currently indistinguishable from a fresh one.
17|
18|## 2. Success criteria (acceptance, from the task)
19|
20|1. Unit test asserting `factsFor()` reports build identity — fails on today's code, passes after.
21|2. `codeChangedSinceBoot` flips to `true` after a file touch (temp-dir fixture).
22|3. `normalizeCapabilities` preserves `versions.build`.
23|4. Settings runner card renders the warning state.
24|5. Release CI rejects an unbumped version when runner code changed.
25|6. No new blocking behavior: mismatch warns only; blocking stays limited to true version
26|   incompatibility (existing `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` path), per survey constraint q15.
27|
28|## 3. Survey inputs (SURVEY.md + round-2 q15)
29|
30|Local `SURVEY.md` (round 1, q1–q5) is **unanswered** (`"answers": {}`), and the referenced
31|`RESPONSE.md` / `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` parent-bug docs are not present in this checkout. The plan
32|therefore adopts the survey's Recommended options as explicit assumptions (flagged for
33|confirmation during implementation):
34|
35|- q1 (what counts as incompatible): runner **major version older than required** → block only
36|  there; everything else warns. Matches existing minimum-version machinery.
37|- q2 (where the warning appears): **Settings runner card only** — no dashboard banner, no
38|  per-task warnings.
39|- q3 (code changed after boot): **warn on the card, keep running** — no auto-restart, no
40|  restart button in this work package (button is a named follow-up, not scope).
41|- q4 (dev/local runners): **show build info everywhere, warn only on managed runners**.
42|  Needs a managed-vs-dev discriminator (see Open questions).
43|- q5 (bump enforcement): **strict — fail the release** if the version was not bumped.
44|- Round-2 q15 (hard constraint from the task): **warn, never block, on version mismatch**
45|  ("Only block stale runners if there is a version incompatibility").
46|
47|## 4. Guiding principle — make the change easy, then make the change
48|
49|The risky parts are discovery (which files the installed runner actually reads, how the backend
50|record carries versions, what "backend sha" means for comparison) and test seams (`factsFor` is
51|currently a private function; runner tests run via `node --test`). So the workflow is:
52|
53|1. **Spikes first** (Phase 0): resolve every unknown that could reshape the design before
54|   writing production code.
55|2. **Seams and fixtures** (Phase 1): extract testable units and fixtures with zero behavior
56|   change — pure refactors covered by the existing suites.
57|3. **The change** (Phase 2): five small vertical slices, each independently testable.
58|4. **Assurance** (Phase 3): acceptance tests, regression gates, docs, WP-B rebase, WP-F handoff.
59|
60|## 5. Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; big unknowns before code)
61|
62|Each spike is time-boxed and ends in a short note in this task folder (or a decision recorded
63|in the implementation PR). No production code here.
64|
65|### Spike 0.1 — Which `version.json` does an installed runner read?
66|
67|- Context: `runner/daemon.js` loads `RUNNER_VERSION`/`RUNNER_API_VERSION` from `./version.json`
68|  beside `daemon.js`, but `scripts/package-runner.mjs` copies `runner/` then stamps
69|  `<stage>/version.json` at the **archive root**. Confirm the installed layout
70|  (`releases/<version>/unpacked/...`) and which file the booted daemon parses.
71|- Outcome: the exact file the packager must stamp with `build { sha, builtAt, dirty }`, and
72|  whether the archive-root `version.json` needs the same stamp. If the two can diverge, the
73|  plan's Phase 2 slices must stamp both or unify them.
74|
75|### Spike 0.2 — How do versions reach the Settings card today?
76|
77|- Trace: heartbeat `facts.versions` → `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`
78|  (currently passes `versions` through unsanitized) → backend runner record
79|  (`runnerVersion` top-level? `facts.versions.runner` nested? `capabilities.versions`?) →
80|  `GET /runners`-style API shape → `describeRunnerVersion()` in
81|  `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js` (reads `runnerVersion`, else
82|  `facts.versions.runner`) → `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` roster/detail.
83|- Outcome: the exact record fields where `build` and `codeChangedSinceBoot` must land to be
84|  renderable, and whether backend persistence changes are needed (backend files are **not** in
85|  the owned-files list — if persistence changes are required, that is a scope escalation to
86|  resolve before Phase 2).
87|
88|### Spike 0.3 — What is "backend sha" for the comparison?
89|
90|- The card must warn when `build.sha != backend sha`. Find the authoritative backend identity:
91|  `api/version.json`? A build-info endpoint? The release manifest commit? `git rev-parse HEAD`
92|  at backend boot?
93|- Outcome: a concrete source (endpoint or field) the frontend can compare against, plus the
94|  old-runner/old-backend fallback (missing `build` → show "unknown", never warn — warn-only
95|  for *known* mismatch).
96|
97|### Spike 0.4 — Managed-vs-dev discriminator (survey q4)
98|
99|- Find how the backend/frontend can tell a managed runner from a dev runner today
100|  (install root? wrapper presence? config flag? runner id pattern?).
101|- Outcome: the discriminator the card uses to suppress warnings on dev runners while still
102|  showing build info. If none exists, the cheapest honest fallback is "warn on all" with the
103|  q4 refinement as a follow-up — do not invent a new registry.
104|
105|### Spike 0.5 — Baseline the heartbeat test surface
106|
107|- Inventory existing coverage: `runner/daemon.test.js` (pins `RUNNER_VERSION` to
108|  `version.json`), `runner/updates-*.test.js`, `api/flow/dispatch` tests for
109|  `normalizeCapabilities`, `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` /
110|  `runnerConfigHelpers.test.js`. Note how tests construct facts today (since `factsFor` is
111|  unexported).
112|- Outcome: the seam design for Phase 1 (export vs. test hook vs. through-public-API tests).
113|
114|## 6. Phase 1 — Make the change easy (zero-behavior-change refactors)
115|
116|Each step must keep all existing suites green. Land as one preparatory commit (or stacked PR)
117|before any behavior change.
118|
119|1. **Extract version loading** in `runner/daemon.js`: move the two `version.json` IIFE reads
120|   into a small pure loader (e.g. `loadRunnerVersionInfo(dir)` returning
121|   `{ runnerVersion, apiVersion, build }`) with `dir` injectable; keep `RUNNER_VERSION` /
122|   `RUNNER_API_VERSION` as thin wrappers. Add unit tests pinning current fallback behavior.
123|2. **Add a `factsFor` test seam**: export `factsFor` for tests (or add an explicit test-hook
124|   export) without changing its output. Add a characterization test snapshotting today's
125|   `versions: { protocol, runner, api }` shape — this is the test that Phase 2 extends into
126|   acceptance criterion 1.
127|3. **Add a temp-dir runner fixture helper** for runner tests: builds a fake `runner/` tree
128|   (with `version.json`) under `os.tmpdir()`, so the mtime-scan tests never touch the real
129|   checkout. Reuse in acceptance criterion 2.
130|4. **Frontend helper seam**: confirm `describeRunnerVersion`-style helpers are the single place
131|   the card reads versions from; add a pure `describeRunnerBuild(runner)` + warning-predicate
132|   helper file alongside with tests for the unknown/missing cases first (old runners send no
133|   `build` — must render "unknown", no warning, no crash).
134|5. **CI script seam**: verify `scripts/detect-changed-components.mjs` already flags
135|   `runner/**` → runner and `api/agent/**` → backend+runner (it does today, including
136|   `api/agent/harnesses/**`); add a test pinning that mapping so the Phase-2 bump gate can
137|   rely on it.
138|
139|Validation after Phase 1: `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` (+ the full runner-release gate
140|list from `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml`), `npm run test:unit`, frontend settings
141|tests — all green, no behavior delta.
142|
143|## 7. Phase 2 — Make the change (five slices, in order)
144|
145|Slice order follows dependency order: identity → signal → passthrough → enforcement → display.
146|Each slice ships with its tests; each is independently revertable except where noted.
147|
148|### Slice 2.1 — Build identity in `runner/version.json` + packager stamping
149|
150|- Extend `runner/version.json` schema with `build: { sha, builtAt, dirty }`
151|  (all nullable/optional for backward compat; checked-in file carries `null`s or is
152|  git-ignored per repo convention — decide in implementation, document it).
153|- `scripts/package-runner.mjs`: stamp `build` at bundle time —
154|  `sha` from `git rev-parse HEAD`, `builtAt` as ISO time, `dirty` from
155|  `git status --porcelain` (scoped to the packaged tree). Stamp the file Spike 0.1 proved is
156|  read (and the archive-root copy if they differ).
157|- `scripts/generate-runner-manifest.mjs`: optionally carry the build sha into the manifest
158|  (so the update channel can compare identities, not just semver) — additive field only.
159|- Dev-runner fallback in `runner/daemon.js`: when the stamped `build.sha` is absent (running
160|  from a git checkout), compute at boot via `git rev-parse HEAD` + dirty from
161|  `git status --porcelain runner/`; best-effort, never fails boot (not-a-checkout →
162|  `sha: null`, `dirty: null`).
163|- Owned files: `runner/version.json`, `scripts/package-runner.mjs`
164|  (+ `scripts/generate-runner-manifest.mjs` if the manifest field is added), `runner/daemon.js`
165|  version-loading block only.
166|
167|### Slice 2.2 — Heartbeat: `build` + `bootedAtMs` + `codeChangedSinceBoot`
168|
169|- Boot: record `bootedAtMs = Date.now()` and hash the `runner/` tree (cheap fingerprint:
170|  max mtime + file count + sizes; full content hash is overkill and slow on every heartbeat).
171|- Per heartbeat in `factsFor()`: re-scan mtimes cheaply (single directory walk, no hashing);
172|  report `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` when any file under `runner/` is newer than boot (or
173|  the fingerprint changed). Guard cost: skip when a previous heartbeat already flipped, or
174|  cache scan results for N seconds.
175|- `facts.versions` becomes `{ protocol, runner, api, build, bootedAtMs, codeChangedSinceBoot }`
176|  (exact nesting per Spike 0.2 — `build` inside `versions` per the task; keep old keys
177|  byte-identical for old backends).
178|- Owned files: `runner/daemon.js` `factsFor()`/`versions` only. **Do not touch
179|  `refreshDiscoveredModels`/boot sequencing — that is WP-B's area.**
180|- Performance note: the mtime walk must be bounded (ignore `node_modules`, logs); add a test
181|  asserting the scan completes fast on a synthetic tree.
182|
183|### Slice 2.3 — `normalizeCapabilities` versions passthrough
184|
185|- `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`: sanitize-and-preserve `versions.build`,
186|  `bootedAtMs`, `codeChangedSinceBoot` following the file's existing advisory-data rule
187|  (malformed → dropped, never a 400 — mirror `sanitizeDiscoveryStatus` bounds: capped
188|  strings, finite numbers, booleans).
189|- Old runners without `build` pass through unchanged (no `build` key, no error).
190|- Acceptance criterion 3 test lives here.
191|
192|### Slice 2.4 — Release pipeline: bump enforcement (strict, per survey q5)
193|
194|- New script (e.g. `scripts/check-runner-version-bump.mjs`): given a base ref (default: last
195|  release commit, same convention as `detect-changed-components.mjs`), fail (exit 1) when
196|  `runner/**` or `api/agent/harnesses/**` changed but `runner/version.json` `runnerVersion`
197|  did not increase (semver-greater than the base's copy).
198|- Wire into `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml` as an early gate step (before packaging),
199|  reusing `detect-changed-components.mjs` path semantics so the two cannot disagree on what
200|  "runner code" means.
201|- Edge cases: first release / missing base (warn, don't fail); pre-release tags (`-rc.N`)
202|  count as increases over the base; `version.json`-only releases pass trivially.
203|- Acceptance criterion 5 test: script-level tests with fixture git ranges (or a `--files`
204|  mode like `detect-changed-components.mjs --files` for hermetic tests) asserting
205|  fail-on-unbumped and pass-on-bumped.
206|
207|### Slice 2.5 — Settings runner card: build sha + warning
208|
209|- `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`: `describeRunnerBuild` (short sha,
210|  dirty marker, built-at) + `runnerBuildWarning(runner, backendSha)` predicate implementing
211|  survey q1–q4: warn on known sha mismatch or `codeChangedSinceBoot`, suppress warnings for
212|  dev runners (Spike 0.4 discriminator), never block.
213|- `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` (roster row + detail panel, exact card TBD by Spike 0.2):
214|  show short sha next to the existing version badge; render a warning banner inline on mismatch
215|  / changed-since-boot. Old runners (no `build`) show "unknown", no warning.
216|- Copy must say what to do ("restart or update this runner") without ever disabling actions —
217|  q15 warn-never-block.
218|- Acceptance criterion 4 test: component test asserting the warning renders for a mismatched
219|  fixture and stays hidden for matching/unknown fixtures.
220|
221|## 8. Phase 3 — Assurance plan
222|
223|### 8.1 Acceptance tests (one per criterion, must fail before / pass after)
224|
225|| # | Test | Location | Fails today because |
226||---|------|----------|---------------------|
227|| 1 | `factsFor()` output includes `versions.build.{sha,builtAt,dirty}` + `bootedAtMs` | `runner/daemon.test.js` | `versions` is only `{protocol,runner,api}` |
228|| 2 | touch a file in temp-dir fixture → next `factsFor()` reports `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` | `runner/daemon.test.js` (fixture from Phase 1.3) | field does not exist |
229|| 3 | `normalizeCapabilities` preserves `versions.build` (and drops malformed advisory values without errors) | dispatch test file for `normalizeCapabilities` | passthrough not implemented (currently raw passthrough — test pins the sanitized shape) |
230|| 4 | warning renders on sha mismatch / `codeChangedSinceBoot`; hidden on match/unknown/dev | `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` + helpers test | no build UI exists |
231|| 5 | bump-check script exits 1 on runner-code-change without version increase; 0 otherwise | new script test (hermetic `--files` mode) | script does not exist |
232|
233|### 8.2 Regression gates (must stay green throughout)
234|
235|- Runner update-channel gate (exact list from `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml`):
236|  `node --test runner/updates-*.test.js runner/config.test.js runner/daemon.test.js`.
237|- Full unit suites: `npm run test:unit` (api + frontend).
238|- Compat gate: `node scripts/check-component-compat.mjs` (version.json schema change must not
239|  break it — `build` is additive).
240|- Old-runner interop: heartbeat fixtures without `build` still normalize and render (covered
241|  by slices 2.3/2.5 negative tests). Old-backend interop: new `versions` keys are ignored, not
242|  rejected (verify against the backend's heartbeat validation tests).
243|
244|### 8.3 Manual / visual verification
245|
246|- Settings card: use the headless screenshot tool (`npm run capture:screenshot`) against a
247|  fixture runner in each state (match / mismatch / changed-since-boot / unknown / dev) —
248|  do not spawn long-lived background servers; use existing mock fixtures or the headless
249|  runner. Eyeball the warning copy and layout per Testing & Verification Guidance.
250|- End-to-end heartbeat check (optional, if a sandbox runner exists): boot a dev runner from
251|  the checkout, confirm `build.sha` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`, touch `runner/daemon.js`,
252|  confirm the next heartbeat carries `codeChangedSinceBoot: true`.
253|
254|### 8.4 Documentation updates
255|
256|- `runner/README.md` (or the runner docs page): document `build` fields, dev-checkout fallback,
257|  and what `codeChangedSinceBoot` means.
258|- Release docs (`docs/PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md` "Runner updates" section, referenced by the
259|  release workflow notes): document the bump requirement and the CI failure message + fix
260|  (bump `runnerVersion`).
261|- Settings/help copy if the UI has inline help for the Runners screen.
262|- This task folder: record Spike 0.1–0.5 outcomes (short notes) so WP-F and reviewers can
263|  follow the decisions.
264|
265|### 8.5 Coordination and sequencing
266|
267|- No blockers to start (spikes are self-contained).
268|- WP-B overlap (`runner/daemon.js`): keep slices 2.1/2.2 clear of `refreshDiscoveredModels`
269|  and boot sequencing; whoever merges second rebases. Prefer landing the Phase-1 extraction
270|  first so both work packages share the seam.
271|- Blocks WP-F: handoff is the shipped `versions.build` / `codeChangedSinceBoot` contract
272|  (field names, types, fallback semantics) — publish it in the PR description and link from
273|  this folder.
274|
275|## 9. Risks and mitigations
276|
277|- **Backend persistence gap** (Spike 0.2 outcome): if the runner record cannot carry `build`
278|  without backend changes outside the owned files, escalate scope before Slice 2.3 — do not
279|  smuggle backend edits into this work package.
280|- **Mtime-scan cost on every heartbeat**: bound the walk (single pass, skip heavy dirs,
281|  short-circuit once flipped); cover with a perf assertion test.
282|- **False positives**: clock skew / reinstalls flipping `codeChangedSinceBoot` — mitigate by
283|  comparing against boot fingerprint rather than wall-clock alone, and keep it warn-only so a
284|  false positive is cosmetic, never operational.
285|- **`git` unavailable in production bundles**: dev fallback must fail soft (`sha: null`);
286|  packaged runners always carry the stamp — CI test asserts the packaged archive contains a
287|  non-null `build.sha`.
288|- **Strict bump gate breaking hotfix flow**: gate fails only when runner-code paths changed
289|  without a version increase; provide a documented override (e.g. explicit label/env) only if
290|  the team asks — default is strict per survey q5.
291|
292|## 10. Non-goals
293|
294|- Auto-restart or restart button on stale detection (survey q3 follow-up).
295|- Dashboard banners or per-task warnings (survey q2 decided: card only).
296|- Blocking stale runners (forbidden by q15 except true incompatibility, which already exists).
297|- Changing `runner/updates` selection logic beyond making version data available.
298|- WP-B scope (`refreshDiscoveredModels`, boot sequencing, model discovery).
299|
300|## 11. Open questions
301|
302|1. SURVEY.md q1–q5 are unanswered — are the Recommended defaults adopted in §3 acceptable?
303|   (Assumption: yes; confirm before Slice 2.4/2.5.)
304|2. Where does the authoritative "backend sha" live? (Spike 0.3.)
305|3. What distinguishes a managed runner from a dev runner for q4 warning suppression?
306|   (Spike 0.4.)
307|4. Should the checked-in `runner/version.json` carry null `build` fields or omit `build`
308|   until stamped? (Decide in Slice 2.1; keep `check-component-compat` green either way.)
309|5. Does the update manifest need the build sha, or is semver comparison sufficient once bumps
310|   are enforced? (Slice 2.1 optional item.)
311|
312|## 12. Work-order summary (earliest first)
313|
314|1. Spikes 0.1–0.5 (research; unblock design decisions).
315|2. Phase 1 seams + characterization tests (safe refactors).
316|3. Slice 2.1 build identity + packager stamping.

@@ -325,3 +325,28 @@ a queued command waits for the next heartbeat, and Update now never

 that predate `facts.commands` ignore the channel; Settings shows manual
 guidance instead of a dead button.
+
+## Build identity and stale-code detection
+
+Every heartbeat reports `versions.build` (`{ sha, builtAt, dirty, source }`),
+`versions.bootedAtMs`, and `versions.codeChangedSinceBoot`:
+
+- Packaged Runners carry the release stamp (`source: "package"`): the
+  commit, bundle time, and tree dirtiness recorded by
+  `scripts/package-runner.mjs` at bundle time.
+- Dev Runners booted from a git checkout compute it at boot instead
+  (`source: "checkout"`): `git rev-parse HEAD` plus dirty from
+  `git status --porcelain` scoped to `runner/`. No bundle time exists for
+  a live checkout, so `builtAt` is null. Outside a checkout with no stamp
+  every field is null ("unknown") — never a boot failure.
+- At boot the daemon fingerprints its own `runner/` tree (file count,
+  bytes, newest mtime); each heartbeat rescans cheaply and reports
+  `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` once any file changes underneath the
+  running process (edits, added/removed files). `.git` and
+  `node_modules` are never scanned.
+
+Settings › Runners shows the short sha next to the version badge and warns
+(warn-only, never a block) when the code changed after boot or when the
+build sha differs from the backend commit. Dev checkouts show their build
+info but never warn. Old Runners without build identity show "unknown"
+with no warning, and old backends ignore the new `versions` keys.

+
+Every heartbeat reports `versions.build` (`{ sha, builtAt, dirty, source }`),
+`versions.bootedAtMs`, and `versions.codeChangedSinceBoot`:
+
+- Packaged Runners carry the release stamp (`source: "package"`): the
+  commit, bundle time, and tree dirtiness recorded by
+  `scripts/package-runner.mjs` at bundle time.

+  (`source: "checkout"`): `git rev-parse HEAD` plus dirty from
+  `git status --porcelain` scoped to `runner/`. No bundle time exists for
+  a live checkout, so `builtAt` is null. Outside a checkout with no stamp
+  every field is null ("unknown") — never a boot failure.
+- At boot the daemon fingerprints its own `runner/` tree (file count,
+  bytes, newest mtime); each heartbeat rescans cheaply and reports
+  `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` once any file changes underneath the
+  running process (edits, added/removed files). `.git` and
+  `node_modules` are never scanned.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the distributable Runner bundle: dist/kainbain-runner-<ref>.tar.gz
#
# Thin wrapper only: the canonical bundle builder is
# scripts/package-runner.mjs (one packager, one layout — the layout the
# self-update channel boots: version.json at the archive root next to
# runner/, api/, shared/). This script keeps the legacy short-sha tarball
# NAME that publish.sh records in dist/release-manifest.json, but the bytes
# inside are exactly what the .mjs builder emits for this host's platform,
# stamped with runner/version.json's runnerVersion.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
REF="${1:-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo dev)}"
VERSION="$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("runner/version.json","utf8")).runnerVersion)')"

## What was reviewed

Task-owned source diff vs merge-base (plus the task docs):

- `runner/version.json`, `scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `scripts/check-runner-version-bump.mjs` (new), `.github/workflows/runner-release.yml`
- `runner/daemon.js` (+ `runner/daemon.test.js`), `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js` (+ test)
- `frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`, `runnerConfigHelpers.js` (+ tests)
- `tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs`, `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs`
- Docs: `runner/README.md`, `docs/PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `SPIKES.md`, `UPDATE_SAFETY_AUDIT.md`, `DOCS_REVIEW.md`

## Goal achievement — yes, all four clauses plus all five acceptance criteria

1. **Build identity stamped at bundle time; dev fallback at boot.** `package-runner.mjs` stamps `build { sha, builtAt, dirty }` into BOTH `version.json` copies (archive root + `runner/` copy the daemon reads — the Spike 0.1 finding). `resolveRunnerBuild()` uses the stamp (`source: "package"`) or computes `git rev-parse HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` scoped to the runner tree at boot (`source: "checkout"`), fail-soft to nulls. `package-runner.sh` (the real `publish.sh` path) is a thin wrapper around the `.mjs`, so the stamp applies to real releases.
2. **Heartbeat signal.** `factsFor()` reports `versions.build` (defensive copy per call), `bootedAtMs`, and `codeChangedSinceBoot` from a boot fingerprint vs per-heartbeat mtime rescan (`snapshotCodeTree`/`hasCodeChangedSinceBoot`, skipping `.git`/`node_modules`, fail-quiet).
3. **Bump enforcement.** New `check-runner-version-bump.mjs` fails when `runner/**` or `api/agent/harnesses/**` changed without a semver increase (test/spec/md + `version.json` itself excluded); wired as the `version-bump-gate` job before packaging. End-to-end flow is coherent: `publish.sh --runner` cuts `runner-v*` from the bumped `runner/version.json` (verified in `publish.sh`), so tag-vs-base-file comparison enforces the bump under the documented flow.
4. **Settings card.** Roster shows `build <shortSha>` (+dirty/dev markers) and a `stale code` badge; detail panel shows build line + warning banner. Warn-only: zero diff lines touch `belowMinimum`/`RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM`/409 paths.

## Verification — ran, not trusted (all green, this session)

- `node --test runner/daemon.test.js`: **140/140** (incl. `factsFor` build-identity test and temp-dir touch→`codeChangedSinceBoot:true` flip test, which uses explicit future `utimes` — not flaky).
- `node --test tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`: **21/21** (incl. real-git-range reject-then-accept and dual-copy stamping through `applyUpdate`).
- API `normalizeCapabilities.test.js` (vitest): **15/15** (build passthrough, old-runner untouched, malformed dropped, future keys pass through).
- Frontend settings tests: **111/111** (build describe/warning helpers + card render/suppress cases).
- `node scripts/check-component-compat.mjs`: all OK (additive `build` key breaks nothing).
- ESLint on changed api/frontend files: **0 errors** (only pre-existing `security/detect-object-injection` warnings in untouched code); new code adds none.
- Corroborated the two spike claims the UI depends on: `RunnerRegistry._public` embeds raw `facts` verbatim (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js:342`) so no backend change was needed, and `GET /status` returns `build` from `deployManager.readBuild()` (`api/routes/status.js:150`, `commit` per `api/deployManager.js:275`).

Screenshots skipped deliberately: the headless tool needs a live app with a staged stale runner; component tests already assert the rendered banner/badge/suppression states, and spinning up servers is out of scope for this review.

## Plan, standards, debt

- **Follows the plan:** all five Phase-2 slices shipped with the designed seams (`loadRunnerVersionInfo`, exported `factsFor` + `codeTree` override, temp-dir fixtures, `--files` hermetic gate mode). Deviations are documented and immaterial (manifest sha skipped as an explicit non-goal; no scan-perf assertion test).
- **Scope discipline:** `runner/daemon.js` diff is version-loading + build/stale helpers + `factsFor().versions` only — no `refreshDiscoveredModels`/boot changes, so the WP-B overlap note holds.
- **Standards:** MARK/JSDoc blocks, functional pure helpers, colocated tests, immutable-per-call heartbeat data. Matches repo conventions.
- **Tech debt:** minimal. Two trivial notes: (a) every heartbeat rescans even after flipping (no flip-cache; negligible at 60s cadence on a small tree); (b) the gate's base version comes from the base tag's file, which relies on the tag==file convention the docs establish — the failure message's "(or retag higher)" path lets a manual higher tag pass without a file bump, but updates still flow since the release version increased.

## Non-blocking observations (for humans, not fail reasons)

1. **Dev-checkout warnings are fully suppressed** (`runnerBuildWarning` returns null for `source === "checkout"`), per unanswered-survey q4's Recommended option adopted as a plan assumption. Note the irony: N1's evidence runner (local-bravo, running from the engine checkout) would show build info but never warn. The `codeChangedSinceBoot` signal still flows in heartbeat facts; only the card warning is suppressed, and checkout churn would otherwise be noise. Worth a product confirm, but the plan/survey/docs/tests are mutually consistent, so not a defect.
2. **Branch hygiene:** the branch also carries engine-auto-committed docs from other tasks (`b8c9bb8e`, `55460086`, `77a4072e`, `9d2b75a2`, `e597e05b` under `docs/tasks/`). Additive and unrelated to this change — leave for merge-time untangling; do not delete here (some may exist only on this branch).
